   > \]

items.title: $(\mathbb{W},+,\cdot,0,1)$ Is a Commutative Semiring
items.statement:
The structure
$(\mathbb{W},+_{\mathbb{W}},\cdot_{\mathbb{W}},0,1)$ is a commutative
semiring.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The structure
   > $(\mathbb{W},+_{\mathbb{W}},\cdot_{\mathbb{W}},0,1)$ is a commutative
   > semiring.

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{W}$ Extends Order on $\mathbb{N}$
items.statement:
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$,
\[
a\leq_{\mathbb{W}}b\Longleftrightarrow a\leq_{\mathbb{N}}b,
\qquad
a<_{\mathbb{W}}b\Longleftrightarrow a<_{\mathbb{N}}b.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$,
   > \[
   > a\leq_{\mathbb{W}}b\Longleftrightarrow a\leq_{\mathbb{N}}b,
   > \qquad
   > a<_{\mathbb{W}}b\Longleftrightarrow a<_{\mathbb{N}}b.
   > \]

items.title: Zero Is the Least Element of $\mathbb{W}$
items.statement:
For every $a\in\mathbb{W}$,
\[
0\leq_{\mathbb{W}}a.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $a\in\mathbb{W}$,
   > \[
   > 0\leq_{\mathbb{W}}a.

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{W}$ Is Total
items.statement:
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$,
\[
a\leq_{\mathbb{W}}b
\quad\text{or}\quad
b\leq_{\mathbb{W}}a.

items.markdown:

items.title: $\mathbb{W}$ Is a Commutative Ordered Semiring
items.statement:
With the operations $+_{\mathbb{W}}$ and $\cdot_{\mathbb{W}}$ and the order
$\le_{\mathbb{W}}$, the whole numbers form a commutative ordered semiring.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > With the operations $+_{\mathbb{W}}$ and $\cdot_{\mathbb{W}}$ and the order
   > $\le_{\mathbb{W}}$, the whole numbers form a commutative ordered semiring.

items.title: Addition on $\mathbb{W}$ Extends Addition on $\mathbb{N}$
items.statement:
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$,
\[
a+_{\mathbb{W}}b=a+_{\mathbb{N}}b.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$,

items.title: $\mathbb{N}$ Embeds into $\mathbb{W}$ as the Positive Part
items.statement:
The inclusion map identifies $\mathbb{N}$ with the positive part
$\mathbb{W}\setminus\{0\}$ and preserves successor, $1$, addition,
multiplication, and order.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The inclusion map identifies $\mathbb{N}$ with the positive part
   > $\mathbb{W}\setminus\{0\}$ and preserves successor, $1$, addition,
   > multiplication, and order.

items.title: $\mathbb{W}$ Has No Additive Inverses Except $0$
items.statement:
If $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$ and
\[
a+_{\mathbb{W}}b=0,
\]
then $a=0$ and $b=0$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$ and
   > \[
   > a+_{\mathbb{W}}b=0,
   > \]
   > then $a=0$ and $b=0$.

items.title: $\mathbb{W}$ Is Not a Ring
items.statement:
With the operations $+_{\mathbb{W}}$ and $\cdot_{\mathbb{W}}$, the whole
numbers do not form a ring.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > With the operations $+_{\mathbb{W}}$ and $\cdot_{\mathbb{W}}$, the whole
   > numbers do not form a ring.

items.title: $0\notin\mathbb{N}$
items.statement:
The adjoined element $0$ is not an element of the one-based natural-number
system:
\[
0\notin\mathbb{N}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The adjoined element $0$ is not an element of the one-based natural-number
   > system:
   > \[
   > 0\notin\mathbb{N}.
   > \]

items.title: Addition on $\mathbb{W}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
The case definition of $+_{\mathbb{W}}$ determines a binary operation on
$\mathbb{W}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The case definition of $+_{\mathbb{W}}$ determines a binary operation on
   > $\mathbb{W}$.

items.title: Left Additive Identity on $\mathbb{W}$
items.statement:
For every $a\in\mathbb{W}$,
\[
0+_{\mathbb{W}}a=a.
\]

> **Statement.**
   > For every $a\in\mathbb{W}$,

   > 0+_{\mathbb{W}}a=a.

items.title: Right Additive Identity on $\mathbb{W}$

For every $a\in\mathbb{W}$,
\[
a+_{\mathbb{W}}0=a.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $a\in\mathbb{W}$,

   > a+_{\mathbb{W}}0=a.

items.title: Addition on $\mathbb{W}$ Satisfies Cancellation
items.statement:
For all $a,b,c\in\mathbb{W}$,
\[
a+_{\mathbb{W}}b=a+_{\mathbb{W}}c\Longrightarrow b=c.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b,c\in\mathbb{W}$,
   > \[
   > a+_{\mathbb{W}}b=a+_{\mathbb{W}}c\Longrightarrow b=c.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication on $\mathbb{W}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
The case definition of $\cdot_{\mathbb{W}}$ determines a binary operation on
$\mathbb{W}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The case definition of $\cdot_{\mathbb{W}}$ determines a binary operation on
   > $\mathbb{W}$.

items.title: Left Zero Absorption on $\mathbb{W}$
items.statement:
For every $a\in\mathbb{W}$,
\[
0\cdot_{\mathbb{W}}a=0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $a\in\mathbb{W}$,
   > \[
   > 0\cdot_{\mathbb{W}}a=0.
   > \]

items.title: Right Zero Absorption on $\mathbb{W}$

For every $a\in\mathbb{W}$,

a\cdot_{\mathbb{W}}0=0.

items.title: Successor on $\mathbb{W}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
The rule defining $S_{\mathbb{W}}$ determines a function
$S_{\mathbb{W}}:\mathbb{W}\to\mathbb{W}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The rule defining $S_{\mathbb{W}}$ determines a function
   > $S_{\mathbb{W}}:\mathbb{W}\to\mathbb{W}$.

items.title: $0$ Is Not a Successor in $\mathbb{W}$
items.statement: There is no $a\in\mathbb{W}$ such that $S_{\mathbb{W}}(a)=0$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > There is no $a\in\mathbb{W}$ such that $S_{\mathbb{W}}(a)=0$.

items.title: Every Nonzero Element of $\mathbb{W}$ Is a Successor
items.statement:
If $a\in\mathbb{W}$ and $a\neq 0$, then there exists
$b\in\mathbb{W}$ such that $a=S_{\mathbb{W}}(b)$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $a\in\mathbb{W}$ and $a\neq 0$, then there exists
   > $b\in\mathbb{W}$ such that $a=S_{\mathbb{W}}(b)$.

items.title: Successor on $\mathbb{W}$ Is Injective
items.statement:
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$,
\[
S_{\mathbb{W}}(a)=S_{\mathbb{W}}(b)\Longrightarrow a=b.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$,
   > \[
   > S_{\mathbb{W}}(a)=S_{\mathbb{W}}(b)\Longrightarrow a=b.
   > \]

items.title: $(\mathbb{W},0,S_{\mathbb{W}})$ Satisfies the Successor Properties
items.statement:
The triple $(\mathbb{W},0,S_{\mathbb{W}})$ satisfies the successor-side
properties:
\[
0\in\mathbb{W},\qquad
S_{\mathbb{W}}:\mathbb{W}\to\mathbb{W},
\]
\[
\neg\exists a\in\mathbb{W}\;(S_{\mathbb{W}}(a)=0),
\qquad
\forall a,b\in\mathbb{W}\;
(S_{\mathbb{W}}(a)=S_{\mathbb{W}}(b)\Longrightarrow a=b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The triple $(\mathbb{W},0,S_{\mathbb{W}})$ satisfies the successor-side
   > properties:
   > \[
   > 0\in\mathbb{W},\qquad
   > S_{\mathbb{W}}:\mathbb{W}\to\mathbb{W},
   > \]
   > \[
   > \neg\exists a\in\mathbb{W}\;(S_{\mathbb{W}}(a)=0),
   > \qquad
   > \forall a,b\in\mathbb{W}\;
   > (S_{\mathbb{W}}(a)=S_{\mathbb{W}}(b)\Longrightarrow a=b).
   > \]

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{W}$ Is Reflexive
items.statement: For every $a\in\mathbb{W}$, $a\leq_{\mathbb{W}}a$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $a\in\mathbb{W}$, $a\leq_{\mathbb{W}}a$.

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{W}$ Is Antisymmetric
items.statement:
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$,
\[
a\leq_{\mathbb{W}}b\ \text{and}\ b\leq_{\mathbb{W}}a
\Longrightarrow a=b.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$,
   > \[
   > a\leq_{\mathbb{W}}b\ \text{and}\ b\leq_{\mathbb{W}}a
   > \Longrightarrow a=b.
   > \]

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{W}$ Is Transitive
items.statement:
For all $a,b,c\in\mathbb{W}$,
\[
a\leq_{\mathbb{W}}b\ \text{and}\ b\leq_{\mathbb{W}}c
\Longrightarrow a\leq_{\mathbb{W}}c.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b,c\in\mathbb{W}$,
   > \[
   > a\leq_{\mathbb{W}}b\ \text{and}\ b\leq_{\mathbb{W}}c
   > \Longrightarrow a\leq_{\mathbb{W}}c.
   > \]

items.title: Well-Ordering Principle for $\mathbb{W}$
items.statement:
Every nonempty subset of $\mathbb{W}$ has a least element with respect to
$\leq_{\mathbb{W}}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every nonempty subset of $\mathbb{W}$ has a least element with respect to
   > $\leq_{\mathbb{W}}$.

items.title: $\mathbb{Z}$ Has No Zero Divisors
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x\cdot y=0 \Longrightarrow x=0 \text{ or } y=0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x\cdot y=0 \Longrightarrow x=0 \text{ or } y=0.
   > \]

items.title: Zero Is Not One in $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
In $\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Z}}\ne 1_{\mathbb{Z}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > In $\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Z}}\ne 1_{\mathbb{Z}}.
   > \]

items.title: Left Distributivity on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x\cdot(y+z)=x\cdot y+x\cdot z.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x\cdot(y+z)=x\cdot y+x\cdot z.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication Respects Formal-Difference Equivalence on the Left
items.statement:
If $[a,b]=[a',b']$, then
\[
[a,b]\cdot[c,d]=[a',b']\cdot[c,d].
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $[a,b]=[a',b']$, then
   > \[
   > [a,b]\cdot[c,d]=[a',b']\cdot[c,d].
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication Respects Formal-Difference Equivalence on the Right
items.statement:
If $[c,d]=[c',d']$, then
\[
[a,b]\cdot[c,d]=[a,b]\cdot[c',d'].
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $[c,d]=[c',d']$, then
   > \[
   > [a,b]\cdot[c,d]=[a,b]\cdot[c',d'].
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication Respects Formal-Difference Equivalence
items.statement:
If $[a,b]=[a',b']$ and $[c,d]=[c',d']$, then
\[
[a,b]\cdot[c,d]=[a',b']\cdot[c',d'].
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $[a,b]=[a',b']$ and $[c,d]=[c',d']$, then
   > \[
   > [a,b]\cdot[c,d]=[a',b']\cdot[c',d'].
   > \]

Multiplication o
n $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Well-Defined

items.title: Multiplication Distributes over Addition on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement: Multiplication distributes over addition on both sides in $\mathbb{Z}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Multiplication distributes over addition on both sides in $\mathbb{Z}$.

items.title: Addition Respects Formal-Difference Equivalence on the Left
Addition Respects Formal-Difference Equivalence on the Right
Addition on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
Addition determines a well-defined binary operation
$\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Addition determines a well-defined binary operation
   > $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$.

items.title: Addition on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Associative
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
(x+y)+z=x+(y+z).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > (x+y)+z=x+(y+z).
   > \]

items.title: Addition on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Commutative
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x+y=y+x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x+y=y+x.
   > \]

items.title: Zero Is a Left Additive Identity on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Z}}+x=x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Z}}+x=x.
   > \]

items.title: Zero Is a Right Additive Identity on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x+0_{\mathbb{Z}}=x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x+0_{\mathbb{Z}}=x.
   > \]

items.title: Zero Is an Additive Identity on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Z}}+x=x
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
x+0_{\mathbb{Z}}=x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Z}}+x=x
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > x+0_{\mathbb{Z}}=x.
   > \]

items.title: Negation on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement: Negation determines a well-defined unary operation $\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Negation determines a well-defined unary operation $\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$.

items.title:
Neg
ation Gives a Left Additive Inverse on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
(-x)+x=0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
\]
items.markdown:
ation Gives a Left Additive Inverse on $\mathbb{Z}$**
   > **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > (-x)+x=0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
   > \]

items.title: Negation Gives a Right Additive Inverse on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x+(-x)=0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x+(-x)=0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
   > \]

items.title: Every Integer Has an Additive Inverse
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$ there exists $y\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
\[
x+y=0_{\mathbb{Z}}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
y+x=0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$ there exists $y\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
   > \[
   > x+y=0_{\mathbb{Z}}
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > y+x=0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{Z}$ Is an Additive Abelian Group
items.statement: The structure $(\mathbb{Z},+,0_{\mathbb{Z}})$ is an abelian group.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The structure $(\mathbb{Z},+,0_{\mathbb{Z}})$ is an abelian group.

items.title: Multiplication on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Associative
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
(x\cdot y)\cdot z=x\cdot(y\cdot z).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > (x\cdot y)\cdot z=x\cdot(y\cdot z).
   > \]

items.title: One Is a Left Multiplicative Identity on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
1_{\mathbb{Z}}\cdot x=x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > 1_{\mathbb{Z}}\cdot x=x.
   > \]

items.title: One Is a Right Multiplicative Identity on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x\cdot 1_{\mathbb{Z}}=x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x\cdot 1_{\mathbb{Z}}=x.
   > \]

items.title: One Is a Multiplicative Identity on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
1_{\mathbb{Z}}\cdot x=x
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
x\cdot 1_{\mathbb{Z}}=x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > 1_{\mathbb{Z}}\cdot x=x
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > x\cdot 1_{\mathbb{Z}}=x.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{Z}$ Is a Multiplicative Commutative Monoid
items.statement: The structure $(\mathbb{Z},\cdot,1_{\mathbb{Z}})$ is a commutative monoid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The structure $(\mathbb{Z},\cdot,1_{\mathbb{Z}})$ is a commutative monoid.

items.title: $\mathbb{Z}$ Is a Commutative Ring
items.statement:
The structure $(\mathbb{Z},+,\cdot,0_{\mathbb{Z}},1_{\mathbb{Z}})$ is a
commutative ring.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The structure $(\mathbb{Z},+,\cdot,0_{\mathbb{Z}},1_{\mathbb{Z}})$ is a
   > commutative ring.

items.title: $\mathbb{Z}$ Is an Integral Domain
items.statement:
The integers form an integral domain: $\mathbb{Z}$ is a commutative ring,
$0\ne 1$, and $\mathbb{Z}$ has no zero divisors.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The integers form an integral domain: $\mathbb{Z}$ is a commutative ring,
   > $0\ne 1$, and $\mathbb{Z}$ has no zero divisors.

items.title: Multiplicative Cancellation on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
z\ne 0 \land z\cdot x=z\cdot y \Longrightarrow x=y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > z\ne 0 \land z\cdot x=z\cdot y \Longrightarrow x=y.
   > \]

items.title: Zero Absorption on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
0\cdot x=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
x\cdot 0=0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > 0\cdot x=0
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > x\cdot 0=0.
   > \]

items.title: Sign Rule on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
(-x)\cdot y=-(x\cdot y)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
x\cdot(-y)=-(x\cdot y).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > (-x)\cdot y=-(x\cdot y)
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > x\cdot(-y)=-(x\cdot y).
   > \]

items.title: Negative One Rule on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
(-1)\cdot x=-x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > (-1)\cdot x=-x.
   > \]

items.title: Product of Negatives on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
(-x)\cdot(-y)=x\cdot y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > (-x)\cdot(-y)=x\cdot y.
   > \]

items.title: Formal-Difference Equivalence Is Reflexive
items.statement:
For every $(a,b)\in\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}(a,b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $(a,b)\in\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}(a,b).
   > \]

items.title: Formal-Difference Equivalence Is Symmetric
items.statement:
For all prepairs $(a,b),(c,d)$,
\[
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}(c,d)
\Longrightarrow
(c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}(a,b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all prepairs $(a,b),(c,d)$,
   > \[
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}(c,d)
   > \Longrightarrow
   > (c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}(a,b).
   > \]

items.title: Formal-Difference Equivalence Is Transitive
items.statement:
For all prepairs $(a,b),(c,d),(e,f)$,
\[
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}(c,d)\land
(c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}(e,f)
\Longrightarrow
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}(e,f).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all prepairs $(a,b),(c,d),(e,f)$,
   > \[
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}(c,d)\land
   > (c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}(e,f)
   > \Longrightarrow
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}(e,f).
   > \]

items.title: Formal-Difference Equivalence Is an Equivalence Relation
items.statement:
The relation $\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}$ is an equivalence relation on
$\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Z}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The relation $\sim_{\mathbb{Z}}$ is an equivalence relation on
   > $\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Z}$.

items.title: Zero Is an Integer
items.statement: The class $0_{\mathbb{Z}}$ is an element of $\mathbb{Z}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The class $0_{\mathbb{Z}}$ is an element of $\mathbb{Z}$.

items.title: One Is an Integer
items.statement: The class $1_{\mathbb{Z}}$ is an element of $\mathbb{Z}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The class $1_{\mathbb{Z}}$ is an element of $\mathbb{Z}$.

items.title: Divisibility Is Reflexive on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $a\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
a\mid a.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $a\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > a\mid a.
   > \]

items.title: Divisibility Is Transitive on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For all $a,b,c\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
a\mid b\land b\mid c \Longrightarrow a\mid c.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b,c\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > a\mid b\land b\mid c \Longrightarrow a\mid c.
   > \]

items.title: One and Negative One Divide Every Integer
items.statement:
For every $a\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
1\mid a
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
(-1)\mid a.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $a\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > 1\mid a
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > (-1)\mid a.
   > \]

items.title: Every Integer Divides Zero
items.statement:
For every $a\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
a\mid 0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $a\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > a\mid 0.
   > \]

items.title: Divisibility Is Compatible with Negation on the Divisor
items.statement:
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
a\mid b \Longleftrightarrow (-a)\mid b.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > a\mid b \Longleftrightarrow (-a)\mid b.
   > \]

items.title: Divisibility Is Compatible with Negation on the Dividend
items.statement:
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
a\mid b \Longleftrightarrow a\mid(-b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > a\mid b \Longleftrightarrow a\mid(-b).
   > \]

items.title: Divisibility Is Compatible with Negation on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
a\mid b \Longleftrightarrow (-a)\mid b \Longleftrightarrow a\mid(-b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > a\mid b \Longleftrightarrow (-a)\mid b \Longleftrightarrow a\mid(-b).
   > \]

items.title: Divisibility Is Compatible with Addition on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For all $a,b,c\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
a\mid b\land a\mid c \Longrightarrow a\mid(b+c).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b,c\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > a\mid b\land a\mid c \Longrightarrow a\mid(b+c).
   > \]

items.title: Divisibility Respects Linear Combinations on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For all $a,b,c,x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
a\mid b\land a\mid c \Longrightarrow a\mid(b\cdot x+c\cdot y).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b,c,x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > a\mid b\land a\mid c \Longrightarrow a\mid(b\cdot x+c\cdot y).
   > \]

items.title: Canonical Form of Integers
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$, exactly one of the following holds:
\[
x=[n,0]\text{ for some nonzero }n\in\mathbb{W},\qquad
x=[0,0],\qquad
x=[0,n]\text{ for some nonzero }n\in\mathbb{W}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$, exactly one of the following holds:
   > \[
   > x=[n,0]\text{ for some nonzero }n\in\mathbb{W},\qquad
   > x=[0,0],\qquad
   > x=[0,n]\text{ for some nonzero }n\in\mathbb{W}.
   > \]

items.title: Sign Trichotomy on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$, exactly one of
\[
x<0,\qquad x=0,\qquad 0<x
\]
holds.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$, exactly one of
   > \[
   > x<0,\qquad x=0,\qquad 0<x
   > \]
   > holds.

items.title: Trichotomy on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$, exactly one of
\[
x<y,\qquad x=y,\qquad y<x
\]
holds.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$, exactly one of
   > \[
   > x<y,\qquad x=y,\qquad y<x
   > \]
   > holds.

items.title: The Units of $\mathbb{Z}$ Are Exactly $\pm1$
items.statement:
An integer $u$ is a unit if and only if
\[
u=1\quad\text{or}\quad u=-1.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > An integer $u$ is a unit if and only if
   > \[
   > u=1\quad\text{or}\quad u=-1.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Not Well-Ordered
items.statement: The ordered set $(\mathbb{Z},\le)$ is not a well-order.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The ordered set $(\mathbb{Z},\le)$ is not a well-order.

items.title: Division Algorithm on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
If $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $b\ne0$, then there exist unique
$q,r\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
\[
a=bq+r
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
0\le r<|b|.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $b\ne0$, then there exist unique
   > $q,r\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
   > \[
   > a=bq+r
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > 0\le r<|b|.
   > \]

items.title: Bezout Identity on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$, there exist $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
\[
\gcd(a,b)=a\cdot x+b\cdot y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$, there exist $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
   > \[
   > \gcd(a,b)=a\cdot x+b\cdot y.
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves Zero
items.statement:
The canonical embedding satisfies
\[
\iota(0_{\mathbb{W}})=0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The canonical embedding satisfies
   > \[
   > \iota(0_{\mathbb{W}})=0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves One
items.statement:
The canonical embedding satisfies
\[
\iota(1_{\mathbb{W}})=1_{\mathbb{Z}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The canonical embedding satisfies
   > \[
   > \iota(1_{\mathbb{W}})=1_{\mathbb{Z}}.
   > \]

items.title: Embedding $\mathbb{W}$ into $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Injective
items.statement:
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$,
\[
\iota(a)=\iota(b)\Longrightarrow a=b.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$,
   > \[
   > \iota(a)=\iota(b)\Longrightarrow a=b.
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves Addition
items.statement:
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$,
\[
\iota(a+b)=\iota(a)+\iota(b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$,
   > \[
   > \iota(a+b)=\iota(a)+\iota(b).
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves Multiplication
items.statement:
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$,
\[
\iota(a\cdot b)=\iota(a)\cdot\iota(b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$,
   > \[
   > \iota(a\cdot b)=\iota(a)\cdot\iota(b).
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves Order
items.statement:
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$
,
\[
a\le b \Longleftrightarrow \iota(a)\le\iota(b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a,b\in\mathbb{W}$
   > ,
   > \[
   > a\le b \Longleftrightarrow \iota(a)\le\iota(b).
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{W}$ Embeds into $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
The map $\iota:\mathbb{W}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is an injective order-preserving
semiring homomorphism.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The map $\iota:\mathbb{W}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is an injective order-preserving
   > semiring homomorphism.

items.title: Subtraction on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
Subtraction determines a well-defined binary operation
$\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Subtraction determines a well-defined binary operation
   > $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$.

items.title: Positivity Respects Formal-Difference Equivalence
items.statement:
If $[a,b]=[a',b']$, then
\[
b<a \Longleftrightarrow b'<a'.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $[a,b]=[a',b']$, then
   > \[
   > b<a \Longleftrightarrow b'<a'.
   > \]

items.title: Positivity on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
The predicate ``$x$ is positive'' is well-defined on equivalence classes in
$\mathbb{Z}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The predicate ``$x$ is positive'' is well-defined on equivalence classes in
   > $\mathbb{Z}$.

items.title: Product of Positives Is Positive
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
0<x\land 0<y \Longrightarrow 0<x\cdot y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > 0<x\land 0<y \Longrightarrow 0<x\cdot y.
   > \]

items.title: Integers Split by Sign
items.statement:
Every integer is nonnegative or the negative of a nonnegative integer, and
the two descriptions overlap only at $0_{\mathbb{Z}}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every integer is nonnegative or the negative of a nonnegative integer, and
   > the two descriptions overlap only at $0_{\mathbb{Z}}$.

items.title: Image of the Embedding Is the Nonnegative Integers
items.statement:
The image of the canonical embedding $\mathbb{W}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is exactly
the set of nonnegative integers.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The image of the canonical embedding $\mathbb{W}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is exactly
   > the set of nonnegative integers.

items.title: Strict Order on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Irreflexive
items.statement: For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$, not $x<x$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$, not $x<x$.

items.title: Strict Order on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Asymmetric
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x<y \Longrightarrow \neg(y<x).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x<y \Longrightarrow \neg(y<x).
   > \]

items.title: Left Addition Preserves Strict Order on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x<y \Longrightarrow z+x<z+y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x<y \Longrightarrow z+x<z+y.
   > \]

items.title: Right Addition Preserves Strict Order on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x<y \Longrightarrow x+z<y+z.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x<y \Longrightarrow x+z<y+z.
   > \]

items.title: Addition Preserves Strict Order on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement: Addition preserves strict order on both sides in $\mathbb{Z}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Addition preserves strict order on both sides in $\mathbb{Z}$.

items.title: Strict Order on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Transitive
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x<y\land y<z \Longrightarrow x<z.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x<y\land y<z \Longrightarrow x<z.
   > \]

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Reflexive
items.statement: For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$, $x\le x$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Z}$, $x\le x$.

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Antisymmetric
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x\le y\land y\le x \Longrightarrow x=y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x\le y\land y\le x \Longrightarrow x=y.
   > \]

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Transitive
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x\le y\land y\le z \Longrightarrow x\le z.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x\le y\land y\le z \Longrightarrow x\le z.
   > \]

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{Z}$ Is Total
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x\le y\text{ or }y\le x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x\le y\text{ or }y\le x.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{Z}$ Is a Totally Ordered Set

items.title: Left Addition Preserves Order on $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x\le y \Longrightarrow z+x\le z+y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$,

items.title: Sign Trichotomy on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$, exactly one of
\[
x<0_{\mathbb{Q}},\qquad x=0_{\mathbb{Q}},\qquad 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x
\]
holds.

   > x<0_{\mathbb{Q}},\qquad x=0_{\mathbb{Q}},\qquad 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x

   > holds.

For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$, exactly one of
\[
x<y,\qquad x=y,\qquad y<x
\]
holds.

> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$, exactly one of
   > \[
   > x<y,\qquad x=y,\qquad y<x
   > \]

\]

items.statement:
For prefractions $(a,b),(c,d)\in\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
[a,b]=[c,d]
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
a\cdot d=b\cdot c.
\]

x\cdot 1_{\mathbb{Q}}=x.

items.statement:
For every prefraction $(a,b)\in\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Q}$,
\[

\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
a=0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
\]

   > \]

items.title: Nonzero Predicate Is Well-Defined on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For every prefraction $(a,b)\in\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
[a,b]\ne 0_{\mathbb{Q}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
a\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
\]
Thus nonzeroness is independent of the representative.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every prefraction $(a,b)\in\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > [a,b]\ne 0_{\mathbb{Q}}
   > \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
   > a\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
   > \]
   > Thus nonzeroness is independent of the representative.

   > x\le y \Longrightarrow x+z\le y+z.
   > \]

items.title: Addition Preserves Order on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement: Addition preserves non-strict order on both sides in $\mathbb{Q}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Addition preserves non-strict order on both sides in $\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title:
Product of Positives Is P
ositive on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x\land 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<y
\Longrightarrow
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x\cdot y.
\]
items.markdown:
ositive on $\mathbb{Q}$**
   > **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x\land 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<y
   > \Longrightarrow
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x\cdot y.
   > \]

items.title:
Left Multiplication by Positives Preserve
s Strict Order on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<z\land x<y
\Longrightarrow
z\cdot x<z\cdot y.
\]
items.markdown:
s Strict Order on $\mathbb{Q}$**
   > **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<z\land x<y
   > \Longrightarrow
   > z\cdot x<z\cdot y.
   > \]

items.title: Left Multiplication by Positives Preserves Order on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<z\land x\le y
\Longrightarrow
z\cdot x\le z\cdot y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<z\land x\le y
   > \Longrightarrow
   > z\cdot x\le z\cdot y.
   > \]

items.title: Right Multiplication by Positives Preserves Strict Order on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<z\land x<y
\Longrightarrow
x\cdot z<y\cdot z.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<z\land x<y
   > \Longrightarrow
   > x\cdot z<y\cdot z.
   > \]

items.title:
Right Multiplication by Positives Preserves Order
 on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<z\land x\le y
\Longrightarrow
x\cdot z\le y\cdot z.
\]
items.markdown:
on $\mathbb{Q}$**
   > **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<z\land x\le y
   > \Longrightarrow
   > x\cdot z\le y\cdot z.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication by Positives Preserves Order on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement: Multiplication by a positive rational preserves non-strict order on both sides.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Multiplication by a positive rational preserves non-strict order on both sides.

items.title: $\mathbb{Q}$ Is an Ordered Field
items.statement:
The structure
\[
(\mathbb{Q},+,\cdot,0_{\mathbb{Q}},1_{\mathbb{Q}},\le)
\]
is an ordered field.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The structure
   > \[
   > (\mathbb{Q},+,\cdot,0_{\mathbb{Q}},1_{\mathbb{Q}},\le)
   > \]
   > is an ordered field.

items.title: One Is Positive in $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
In $\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<1_{\mathbb{Q}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > In $\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<1_{\mathbb{Q}}.
   > \]

items.title: Two Is Nonzero in $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
In $\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
2_{\mathbb{Q}}\ne 0_{\mathbb{Q}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > In $\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 2_{\mathbb{Q}}\ne 0_{\mathbb{Q}}.
   > \]

items.title: Midpoint Lies Strictly Between Rationals
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
x<y
\Longrightarrow
x< (x+y)\cdot 2_{\mathbb{Q}}^{-1}<y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > x<y
   > \Longrightarrow
   > x< (x+y)\cdot 2_{\mathbb{Q}}^{-1}<y.
   > \]

items.title: Density of $\mathbb{Q}$ in Itself
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
x<y
\Longrightarrow
\exists r\in\mathbb{Q}\ (x<r<y).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > x<y
   > \Longrightarrow
   > \exists r\in\mathbb{Q}\ (x<r<y).
   > \]

items.title: Archimedean Property of $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x
\Longrightarrow
\exists n\in\mathbb{N}\ (y<n\cdot x).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x
   > \Longrightarrow
   > \exists n\in\mathbb{N}\ (y<n\cdot x).
   > \]

items.title: Sign of a Reciprocal on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For every nonzero $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x \Longrightarrow 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x^{-1},
\qquad
x<0_{\mathbb{Q}} \Longrightarrow x^{-1}<0_{\mathbb{Q}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every nonzero $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x \Longrightarrow 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x^{-1},
   > \qquad
   > x<0_{\mathbb{Q}} \Longrightarrow x^{-1}<0_{\mathbb{Q}}.
   > \]

items.title: Reciprocals Become Arbitrarily Small in $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For every $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<\varepsilon
\Longrightarrow
\exists n\in\mathbb{N}\ 
\left(0_{\mathbb{Q}}<n^{-1}<\varepsilon\right).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<\varepsilon
   > \Longrightarrow
   > \exists n\in\mathbb{N}\
   > \left(0_{\mathbb{Q}}<n^{-1}<\varepsilon\right).
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{Q}$ Has Arbitrarily Close Distinct Points
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$ and every $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<\varepsilon
\Longrightarrow
\exists y\in\mathbb{Q}\ (y\ne x\ \text{and}\ |x-y|<\varepsilon).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$ and every $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<\varepsilon
   > \Longrightarrow
   > \exists y\in\mathbb{Q}\ (y\ne x\ \text{and}\ |x-y|<\varepsilon).
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{Q}$ Has No Adjacent Points
items.statement:
There do not exist rational numbers $x<y$ with no rational number strictly
between them.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > There do not exist rational numbers $x<y$ with no rational number strictly
   > between them.

items.title: $\mathbb{Q}$ Has No Least Positive Rational
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x
\Longrightarrow
\exists y\in\mathbb{Q}\ (0_{\mathbb{Q}}<y<x).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x
   > \Longrightarrow
   > \exists y\in\mathbb{Q}\ (0_{\mathbb{Q}}<y<x).
   > \]

items.title: One-Sided Rational Approximation
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$ and every $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<\varepsilon
\Longrightarrow
\exists y,z\in\mathbb{Q}\ (x-\varepsilon<y<x<z<x+\varepsilon).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$ and every $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<\varepsilon
   > \Longrightarrow
   > \exists y,z\in\mathbb{Q}\ (x-\varepsilon<y<x<z<x+\varepsilon).
   > \]

items.title: Fraction Equivalence Is Reflexive
items.statement:
For every $(a,b)\in\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}(a,b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $(a,b)\in\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}(a,b).
   > \]

items.title: Fraction Equivalence Is Symmetric
items.statement:
For all prefractions $(a,b),(c,d)$,
\[
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}(c,d)
\Longrightarrow
(c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}(a,b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all prefractions $(a,b),(c,d)$,
   > \[
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}(c,d)
   > \Longrightarrow
   > (c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}(a,b).
   > \]

items.title: Fraction Equivalence Is Transitive
items.statement:
For all prefractions $(a,b),(c,d),(e,f)$,
\[
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}(c,d)\land
(c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}(e,f)
\Longrightarrow
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}(e,f).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all prefractions $(a,b),(c,d),(e,f)$,
   > \[
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}(c,d)\land
   > (c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}(e,f)
   > \Longrightarrow
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}(e,f).
   > \]

items.title: Fraction Equivalence Is an Equivalence Relation
items.statement:
The relation $\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is an equivalence relation on
$\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Q}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The relation $\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is an equivalence relation on
   > $\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: Zero Is a Rational
items.statement: The class $0_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is an element of $\mathbb{Q}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The class $0_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is an element of $\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: One Is a Rational
items.statement: The class $1_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is an element of $\mathbb{Q}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The class $1_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is an element of $\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: Embedding Preserves Zero
items.statement:
The embedding sends integer zero to rational zero:
\[
\iota(0_{\mathbb{Z}})=0_{\mathbb{Q}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The embedding sends integer zero to rational zero:
   > \[
   > \iota(0_{\mathbb{Z}})=0_{\mathbb{Q}}.
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves One
items.statement:
The embedding sends integer one to rational one:
\[
\iota(1_{\mathbb{Z}})=1_{\mathbb{Q}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The embedding sends integer one to rational one:
   > \[
   > \iota(1_{\mathbb{Z}})=1_{\mathbb{Q}}.
   > \]

items.title: Embedding $\mathbb{Z}$ into $\mathbb{Q}$ Is Injective
items.statement:
For all $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
\iota(m)=\iota(n)\Longrightarrow m=n.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > \iota(m)=\iota(n)\Longrightarrow m=n.
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves Addition
items.statement:
For all $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
\iota(m+n)=\iota(m)+\iota(n).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > \iota(m+n)=\iota(m)+\iota(n).
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves Multiplication
items.statement:
For all $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
\iota(m\cdot n)=\iota(m)\cdot\iota(n).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > \iota(m\cdot n)=\iota(m)\cdot\iota(n).
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves Order
items.statement:
For all $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
m\le n
\Longleftrightarrow
\iota(m)\le\iota(n).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > m\le n
   > \Longleftrightarrow
   > \iota(m)\le\iota(n).
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{Z}$ Embeds into $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
The map $\iota:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Q}$ is an injective order-preserving ring
homomorphism.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The map $\iota:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Q}$ is an injective order-preserving ring
   > homomorphism.

items.title: $\mathbb{Q}$ Is the Field of Fractions of $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$, there exist $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$ with
$n\ne0_{\mathbb{Z}}$ such that
\[
x=\iota(m)\cdot \iota(n)^{-1}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$, there exist $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$ with
   > $n\ne0_{\mathbb{Z}}$ such that
   > \[
   > x=\iota(m)\cdot \iota(n)^{-1}.
   > \]

items.title: The Embedding of $\mathbb{Z}$ into $\mathbb{Q}$ Is Not Surjective
items.statement:
The image of $\iota:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Q}$ is a proper subset of
\(\mathbb{Q}\).
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The image of $\iota:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Q}$ is a proper subset of
   > \(\mathbb{Q}\).

items.title: Zero Product on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
x\cdot y=0_{\mathbb{Q}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x=0_{\mathbb{Q}}\ \text{or}\ y=0_{\mathbb{Q}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > x\cdot y=0_{\mathbb{Q}}
   > \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
   > x=0_{\mathbb{Q}}\ \text{or}\ y=0_{\mathbb{Q}}.
   > \]

items.title: Double Negation on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
-(-x)=x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > -(-x)=x.
   > \]

items.title: Negation of a Product on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
(-x)\cdot y=-(x\cdot y)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
x\cdot(-y)=-(x\cdot y).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > (-x)\cdot y=-(x\cdot y)
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > x\cdot(-y)=-(x\cdot y).
   > \]

items.title: Product of Negatives on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
(-x)\cdot(-y)=x\cdot y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > (-x)\cdot(-y)=x\cdot y.
   > \]

items.title: Additive Cancellation on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
x+z=y+z
\Longrightarrow
x=y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > x+z=y+z
   > \Longrightarrow
   > x=y.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplicative Cancellation on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
z\ne 0_{\mathbb{Q}}\land x\cdot z=y\cdot z
\Longrightarrow
x=y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > z\ne 0_{\mathbb{Q}}\land x\cdot z=y\cdot z
   > \Longrightarrow
   > x=y.
   > \]

items.title: Uniqueness of Additive Inverses on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement: Every additive inverse in $\mathbb{Q}$ is unique.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every additive inverse in $\mathbb{Q}$ is unique.

items.title: Uniqueness of Multiplicative Inverses on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement: Every multiplicative inverse of a nonzero rational number is unique.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every multiplicative inverse of a nonzero rational number is unique.

items.title: The Inverse of One Is One on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
In $\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
1_{\mathbb{Q}}^{-1}=1_{\mathbb{Q}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > In $\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 1_{\mathbb{Q}}^{-1}=1_{\mathbb{Q}}.
   > \]

items.title: Inverse of a Product on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all nonzero $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
(x\cdot y)^{-1}=x^{-1}\cdot y^{-1}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all nonzero $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > (x\cdot y)^{-1}=x^{-1}\cdot y^{-1}.
   > \]

items.title: Inverse of an Inverse on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For every nonzero $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
(x^{-1})^{-1}=x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every nonzero $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > (x^{-1})^{-1}=x.
   > \]

items.title: Exponent Addition Law on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For every nonzero $x\in\mathbb{Q}$ and all $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
x^{m+n}=x^m\cdot x^n.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every nonzero $x\in\mathbb{Q}$ and all $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > x^{m+n}=x^m\cdot x^n.
   > \]

items.title: Power of a Power on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For every nonzero $x\in\mathbb{Q}$ 
and all $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
(x^m)^n=x^{m\cdot n}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every nonzero $x\in\mathbb{Q}$
   > and all $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > (x^m)^n=x^{m\cdot n}.
   > \]

items.title: Power of a Product on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all nonzero $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$ and every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
(x\cdot y)^n=x^n\cdot y^n.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all nonzero $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$ and every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$,
   > \[
   > (x\cdot y)^n=x^n\cdot y^n.
   > \]

items.title: Addition Lands in $\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
If $b\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $d\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}$, then
\[
b\cdot d\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $b\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $d\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}$, then
   > \[
   > b\cdot d\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
   > \]

items.title: Subtraction on $\mathbb{Q}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
Subtraction determines a well-defined binary operation
$\mathbb{Q}\times\mathbb{Q}\to\mathbb{Q}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Subtraction determines a well-defined binary operation
   > $\mathbb{Q}\times\mathbb{Q}\to\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: Multiplication Lands in $\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
If $b\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $d\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}$, then
\[
b\cdot d\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $b\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $d\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}$, then
   > \[
   > b\cdot d\ne 0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
   > \]

items.title: Division on $\mathbb{Q}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
Division determines a well-defined map
\[
\mathbb{Q}\times(\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0_{\mathbb{Q}}\})\to\mathbb{Q}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Division determines a well-defined map
   > \[
   > \mathbb{Q}\times(\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{0_{\mathbb{Q}}\})\to\mathbb{Q}.
   > \]

items.title: Positivity Respects Fraction Equivalence on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
If $[a,b]=[c,d]$, then
\[
a\cdot b>0_{\mathbb{Z}}
\Longleftrightarrow
c\cdot d>0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $[a,b]=[c,d]$, then
   > \[
   > a\cdot b>0_{\mathbb{Z}}
   > \Longleftrightarrow
   > c\cdot d>0_{\mathbb{Z}}.
   > \]

items.title: Positivity on $\mathbb{Q}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
The predicate ``$x$ is positive'' is well-defined on equivalence classes in
$\mathbb{Q}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The predicate ``$x$ is positive'' is well-defined on equivalence classes in
   > $\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: Strict Order on $\mathbb{Q}$ Is Irreflexive
items.statement: For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$, not $x<x$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$, not $x<x$.

items.title: Addition Reflects Order on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
Addition by a fixed rational reflects
 both strict and non-strict order.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Addition by a fixed rational reflects
   >  both strict and non-strict order.

items.title: Multiplication by Positives Preserves Strict Order on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement: Multiplication by a positive rational preserves strict order on both sides.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Multiplication by a positive rational preserves strict order on both sides.

items.title: Multiplication by Negatives Reverses Strict Order on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
z<0_{\mathbb{Q}}\land x<y
\Longrightarrow
z\cdot y<z\cdot x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > z<0_{\mathbb{Q}}\land x<y
   > \Longrightarrow
   > z\cdot y<z\cdot x.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication by Negatives Reverses Order on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
z<0_{\mathbb{Q}}\land x\le y
\Longrightarrow
z\cdot y\le z\cdot x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > z<0_{\mathbb{Q}}\land x\le y
   > \Longrightarrow
   > z\cdot y\le z\cdot x.
   > \]

items.title: Reciprocal Reverses Order on Positives in $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x<y
\Longrightarrow
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<y^{-1}<x^{-1}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x<y
   > \Longrightarrow
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<y^{-1}<x^{-1}.
   > \]

items.title: Reciprocal Reverses Order on Same-Sign Rationals
items.statement:
For all nonzero $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x<y
\Longrightarrow
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<y^{-1}<x^{-1},
\qquad
x<y<0_{\mathbb{Q}}
\Longrightarrow
y^{-1}<x^{-1}<0_{\mathbb{Q}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all nonzero $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x<y
   > \Longrightarrow
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<y^{-1}<x^{-1},
   > \qquad
   > x<y<0_{\mathbb{Q}}
   > \Longrightarrow
   > y^{-1}<x^{-1}<0_{\mathbb{Q}}.
   > \]

items.title: Absolute Value Is Nonnegative on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}\le |x|.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}\le |x|.
   > \]

items.title:
Absolute
 Value Vanishes Only at Zero on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
|x|=0_{\mathbb{Q}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x=0_{\mathbb{Q}}.
\]
items.markdown:
Value Vanishes Only at Zero on $\mathbb{Q}$**
   > **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > |x|=0_{\mathbb{Q}}
   > \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
   > x=0_{\mathbb{Q}}.
   > \]

items.title: Absolute Value Is Multiplicative on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
|x\cdot y|=|x|\cdot |y|.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > |x\cdot y|=|x|\cdot |y|.
   > \]

items.title: Triangle Inequality on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
|x+y|\le |x|+|y|.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > |x+y|\le |x|+|y|.
   > \]

items.title: Absolute Value of a Reciprocal on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For every nonzero $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
|x^{-1}|=|x|^{-1}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every nonzero $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > |x^{-1}|=|x|^{-1}.
   > \]

items.title: Ordered Field Laws Hold on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
Every theorem that depends only on the ordered-field axioms applies to
$\mathbb{Q}$ with its constructed operations and order.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every theorem that depends only on the ordered-field axioms applies to
   > $\mathbb{Q}$ with its constructed operations and order.

items.title: Squares Are Nonnegative on $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}\le x^2.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}\le x^2.
   > \]

items.title: Natural Numbers Are Positive in $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement: Every natural number embedded in $\mathbb{Q}$ is positive.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every natural number embedded in $\mathbb{Q}$ is positive.

items.title: Positive Rationals Have Positive Inverses
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x
\Longrightarrow
0_{\mathbb{Q}}
<x^{-1}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}<x
   > \Longrightarrow
   > 0_{\mathbb{Q}}
   > <x^{-1}.
   > \]

items.title: Fraction Comparison in $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement:
For rational classes with positive denominator product,
\[
[a,b]<[c,d]
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
a\cdot d<c\cdot b.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For rational classes with positive denominator product,
   > \[
   > [a,b]<[c,d]
   > \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
   > a\cdot d<c\cdot b.
   > \]

items.title: No Rational Square Root of Two
items.statement:
There is no rational number $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ such that
\[
q\cdot q=2_{\mathbb{Q}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > There is no rational number $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ such that
   > \[
   > q\cdot q=2_{\mathbb{Q}}.
   > \]

items.title: The Gap Set Is Bounded Above in $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement: The set $S$ is nonempty and bounded above in $\mathbb{Q}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The set $S$ is nonempty and bounded above in $\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: The Square-Two Gap Has No Rational Supremum
items.statement: The set $S$ has no least upper bound in $\mathbb{Q}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The set $S$ has no least upper bound in $\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: $\mathbb{Q}$ Is Order-Incomplete
items.statement:
The ordered field $\mathbb{Q}$ is not order-complete: there exists a nonempty
bounded-above subset of $\mathbb{Q}$ with no supremum in $\mathbb{Q}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The ordered field $\mathbb{Q}$ is not order-complete: there exists a nonempty
   > bounded-above subset of $\mathbb{Q}$ with no supremum in $\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: Rational Limits Are Unique
items.statement: A convergent sequence in $\mathbb{Q}$ has at most one rational limit.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > A convergent sequence in $\mathbb{Q}$ has at most one rational limit.

items.title: Characterization of Intervals
items.statement:
A subset $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ is an interval if and only if for all $x,z\in I$
with $x<z$,
\[
[x,z]\subseteq I.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > A subset $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ is an interval if and only if for all $x,z\in I$
   > with $x<z$,
   > \[
   > [x,z]\subseteq I.
   > \]

items.title: Classification of Intervals in $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
Every interval in $\mathbb{R}$ is one of the standard interval types:
\[
(a,b),\ [a,b],\ (a,b],\ [a,b),\ (a,\infty),\ [a,\infty),
\]
\[
(-\infty,b),\ (-\infty,b],\ \mathbb{R},\ \varnothing,
\]
including degenerate one-point intervals.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every interval in $\mathbb{R}$ is one of the standard interval types:
   > \[
   > (a,b),\ [a,b],\ (a,b],\ [a,b),\ (a,\infty),\ [a,\infty),
   > \]
   > \[
   > (-\infty,b),\ (-\infty,b],\ \mathbb{R},\ \varnothing,
   > \]
   > including degenerate one-point intervals.

items.title: Sum of Cuts Is a Cut
items.statement: If $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is a Dedekind cut.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is a Dedekind cut.

items.title: Addition on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Associative
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
(\alpha+\beta)+\gamma=\alpha+(\beta+\gamma).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > (\alpha+\beta)+\gamma=\alpha+(\beta+\gamma).
   > \]

items.title: Addition on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Commutative
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha+\beta=\beta+\alpha.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha+\beta=\beta+\alpha.
   > \]

items.title: Zero Is an Additive Identity on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha+0_{\mathbb{R}}=\alpha.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha+0_{\mathbb{R}}=\alpha.
   > \]

items.title: Negation of a Cut Is a Cut
items.statement: If $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, then $-\alpha$ is a Dedekind cut.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, then $-\alpha$ is a Dedekind cut.

items.title: Negation Is an Additive Inverse on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha+(-\alpha)=0_{\mathbb{R}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha+(-\alpha)=0_{\mathbb{R}}.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Is an Additive Abelian Group
items.statement:
The structure
 $(\mathbb{R},+,0_{\mathbb{R}})$ is an abelian group.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The structure
   >  $(\mathbb{R},+,0_{\mathbb{R}})$ is an abelian group.

items.title: Union of a Bounded Nonempty Family of Cuts Is a Cut
items.statement:
If $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ is nonempty and bounded above, then
\[
\bigcup_{\alpha\in S}\alpha
\]
is a Dedekind cut.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ is nonempty and bounded above, then
   > \[
   > \bigcup_{\alpha\in S}\alpha
   > \]
   > is a Dedekind cut.

items.title: Least-Upper-Bound Property
items.statement:
Every nonempty subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ that is bounded above has a least
upper bound, namely
\[
\sup S=\bigcup_{\alpha\in S}\alpha.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every nonempty subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ that is bounded above has a least
   > upper bound, namely
   > \[
   > \sup S=\bigcup_{\alpha\in S}\alpha.
   > \]

items.title: Zero Is Not One in $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
In $\mathbb{R}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{R}}\ne 1_{\mathbb{R}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > In $\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{R}}\ne 1_{\mathbb{R}}.
   > \]

items.title: Product of Nonnegative Cuts Is a Cut
items.statement: If $\alpha,\beta\ge 0_{\mathbb{R}}$, then $\alpha\cdot\beta$ is a Dedekind cut.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $\alpha,\beta\ge 0_{\mathbb{R}}$, then $\alpha\cdot\beta$ is a Dedekind cut.

items.title: Product of Cuts Is a Cut
items.statement: If $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\alpha\cdot\beta\in\mathbb{R}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\alpha\cdot\beta\in\mathbb{R}$.

items.title: Multiplication on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Associative
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
(\alpha\cdot\beta)\cdot\gamma=\alpha\cdot(\beta\cdot\gamma).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > (\alpha\cdot\beta)\cdot\gamma=\alpha\cdot(\beta\cdot\gamma).
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Commutative
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\cdot\beta=\beta\cdot\alpha.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\cdot\beta=\beta\cdot\alpha.
   > \]

items.title: One Is a Multiplicative Identity on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\cdot 1_{\mathbb{R}}=\alpha.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\cdot 1_{\mathbb{R}}=\alpha.
   > \]

items.title: Reciprocal of a Nonzero Cut Is a Cut
items.statement:
If $\alpha\ne0_{\mathbb{R}}$, then $\alpha^
{-1}\in\mathbb{R}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $\alpha\ne0_{\mathbb{R}}$, then $\alpha^
   > {-1}\in\mathbb{R}$.

items.title: Reciprocal Is a Multiplicative Inverse on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
If $\alpha\ne0_{\mathbb{R}}$, then
\[
\alpha\cdot\alpha^{-1}=1_{\mathbb{R}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $\alpha\ne0_{\mathbb{R}}$, then
   > \[
   > \alpha\cdot\alpha^{-1}=1_{\mathbb{R}}.
   > \]

items.title: Nonzero $\mathbb{R}$ Is a Multiplicative Abelian Group
items.statement:
The structure $(\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0_{\mathbb{R}}\},\cdot,1_{\mathbb{R}})$
is an abelian group.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The structure $(\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0_{\mathbb{R}}\},\cdot,1_{\mathbb{R}})$
   > is an abelian group.

items.title: Distributivity on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\cdot(\beta+\gamma)=\alpha\cdot\beta+\alpha\cdot\gamma.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\cdot(\beta+\gamma)=\alpha\cdot\beta+\alpha\cdot\gamma.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Is a Field
items.statement: The structure $(\mathbb{R},+,\cdot,0_{\mathbb{R}},1_{\mathbb{R}})$ is a field.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The structure $(\mathbb{R},+,\cdot,0_{\mathbb{R}},1_{\mathbb{R}})$ is a field.

items.title: Addition Preserves Order on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha<\beta \Longrightarrow \alpha+\gamma<\beta+\gamma,
\]
and the corresponding non-strict statement also holds.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha<\beta \Longrightarrow \alpha+\gamma<\beta+\gamma,
   > \]
   > and the corresponding non-strict statement also holds.

items.title: Multiplication by Positives Preserves Order on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{R}}<\gamma\land\alpha<\beta
\Longrightarrow
\gamma\cdot\alpha<\gamma\cdot\beta.
\]
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{R}}<\gamma\land\alpha<\beta
   > \Longrightarrow
   > \gamma\cdot\alpha<\gamma\cdot\beta.
   > \]

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Reflexive
items.statement: For every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, $\alpha\le\alpha$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, $\alpha\le\alpha$.

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Antisymmetric
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\le\beta\land\beta\le\alpha \Longrightarrow \alpha=\beta.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\le\beta\land\beta\le\alpha \Longrightarrow \alpha=\beta.
   > \]

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Transitive
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\le\beta\land\beta\le\gamma \Longrightarrow \alpha\le\gamma.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\le\beta\land\beta\le\gamma \Longrightarrow \alpha\le\gamma.
   > \]

items.title: Comparability of Cuts
items.statement:
For all cuts $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\subseteq\beta \lor \beta\subseteq\alpha.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all cuts $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\subseteq\beta \lor \beta\subseteq\alpha.
   > \]

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Total
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\le\beta\lor\beta\le\alpha.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\le\beta\lor\beta\le\alpha.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Is a Totally Ordered Set
items.statement: The ordered pair $(\mathbb{R},\le)$ is a total order.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The ordered pair $(\mathbb{R},\le)$ is a total order.

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Is an Ordered Field
items.statement:
The structure $(\mathbb{R},+,\cdot,0_{\mathbb{R}},1_{\mathbb{R}},\le)$ is an
ordered field.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The structure $(\mathbb{R},+,\cdot,0_{\mathbb{R}},1_{\mathbb{R}},\le)$ is an
   > ordered field.

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Is a Complete Ordered Field
items.statement: The ordered field $\mathbb{R}$ satisfies the least-upper-bound property.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The ordered field $\mathbb{R}$ satisfies the least-upper-bound property.

items.title: Uniqueness of the Complete Ordered Field
items.statement: Any two complete ordered fields are isomorphic by a unique order-isomorphism.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Any two complete ordered fields are isomorphic by a unique order-isomorphism.

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Is the Real Numbers
items.statement:
The field $\mathbb{R}$ is determined up to unique order-isomorphism by being a
complete ordered field.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The field $\mathbb{R}$ is determined up to unique order-isomorphism by being a
   > complete ordered field.

items.title: Greatest-Lower-Bound Property
items.statement:
Every nonempty subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ that is bounded below has a
greatest lower bound.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every nonempty subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ that is bounded below has a
   > greatest lower bound.

items.title: Rational Cuts Are Cuts
items.statement: For every $q\in\mathbb{Q}$, the set $q^{\ast}$ is a Dedekind cut.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $q\in\mathbb{Q}$, the set $q^{\ast}$ is a Dedekind cut.

items.title: Zero and One Are Reals
items.statement: The cuts $0_{\mathbb{R}}$ and $1_{\mathbb{R}}$ are elements of $\mathbb{R}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The cuts $0_{\mathbb{R}}$ and $1_{\mathbb{R}}$ are elements of $\mathbb{R}$.

items.title: Embedding Preserves Zero and One
items.statement:
The embedding satisfies
\[
\iota(0_{\mathbb{Q}})=0_{\mathbb{R}}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\iota(1_{\mathbb{Q}})=1_{\mathbb{R}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The embedding satisfies
   > \[
   > \iota(0_{\mathbb{Q}})=0_{\mathbb{R}}
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > \iota(1_{\mathbb{Q}})=1_{\mathbb{R}}.
   > \]

items.title: Embedding $\mathbb{Q}$ into $\mathbb{R}$ Is Injective
items.statement:
For all $p,q\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
\iota(p)=\iota(q) \Longrightarrow p=q.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $p,q\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > \iota(p)=\iota(q) \Longrightarrow p=q.
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves Addition and Multiplication
items.statement:
For all $p,q\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
\iota(p+q)=\iota(p)+\iota(q)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\iota(p\cdot q)=\iota(p)\cdot\iota(q).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $p,q\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > \iota(p+q)=\iota(p)+\iota(q)
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > \iota(p\cdot q)=\iota(p)\cdot\iota(q).
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves Order
items.statement:
For all $p,q\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
p\le q \Longleftrightarrow \iota(p)\le\iota(q).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $p,q\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > p\le q \Longleftrightarrow \iota(p)\le\iota(q).
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{Q}$ Embeds into $\mathbb{R}$ as an Ordered Field
items.statement: The map $\iota$ is an injective order-preserving field homomorphism.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The map $\iota$ is an injective order-preserving field homomorphism.

items.title: Density of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha<\beta \Longrightarrow \exists q\in\mathbb{Q}\,(\alpha<\iota(q)<\beta).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha<\beta \Longrightarrow \exists q\in\mathbb{Q}\,(\alpha<\iota(q)<\beta).
   > \]

items.title: Archimedean Property of $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{R}}<\alpha
\Longrightarrow
\exists n\in\mathbb{N}\,(\beta<\iota(n)\cdot\alpha).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{R}}<\alpha
   > \Longrightarrow
   > \exists n\in\mathbb{N}\,(\beta<\iota(n)\cdot\alpha).
   > \]

items.title: Field Laws Hold on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
Every theorem proved generically for fields holds in $\mathbb{R}$, including
zero product, double negation, sign rules, cancellation, uniqueness of
inverses, inverse laws, and exponent laws.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every theorem proved generically for fields holds in $\mathbb{R}$, including
   > zero product, double negation, sign rules, cancellation, uniqueness of
   > inverses, inverse laws, and exponent laws.

items.title: Ordered-Field Laws Hold on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement: Every theorem proved generically for ordered fields holds in $\mathbb{R}$.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every theorem proved generically for ordered fields holds in $\mathbb{R}$.

items.title: Triangle Inequality
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
|\alpha+\beta|\le |\alpha|+|\beta|.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > |\alpha+\beta|\le |\alpha|+|\beta|.
   > \]

items.title: Trichotomy on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, exactly one of
\[
\alpha<\beta,\qquad \alpha=\beta,\qquad \beta<\alpha
\]
holds.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, exactly one of
   > \[
   > \alpha<\beta,\qquad \alpha=\beta,\qquad \beta<\alpha
   > \]
   > holds.

items.title: Existence of Square Roots
items.statement:
For every real number $a\ge 0$, there exists $x\in\mathbb{R}$ such that
\[
x\ge 0
\quad\text{and}\quad
x^2=a.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every real number $a\ge 0$, there exists $x\in\mathbb{R}$ such that
   > \[
   > x\ge 0
   > \quad\text{and}\quad
   > x^2=a.
   > \]

items.title: Uniqueness of Nonnegative Square Roots
items.statement:
If $x,y\ge 0$ and
\[
x^2=y^2,
\]
then
\[
x=y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $x,y\ge 0$ and
   > \[
   > x^2=y^2,
   > \]
   > then
   > \[
   > x=y.
   > \]

items.title: The Square-Root-of-Two Cut Is a Cut
items.statement: The set $\sqrt{2}$ is a Dedekind cut.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The set $\sqrt{2}$ is a Dedekind cut.

items.title: Its Square Is Two
items.statement:
In $\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}=2_{\mathbb{R}},
\]
where $2_{\mathbb{R}}:=\iota(2_{\mathbb{Q}})$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > In $\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}=2_{\mathbb{R}},
   > \]
   > where $2_{\mathbb{R}}:=\iota(2_{\mathbb{Q}})$.

items.title: Square Root of Two Is Irrational
items.statement:
\[
\sqrt2\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > \[
   > \sqrt2\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Contains the Supremum $\mathbb{Q}$ Was Missing
items.statement:
Let
\[
S=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:0_{\mathbb{Q}}<q\land q\cdot q<2_{\mathbb{Q}}\}.
\]
Then
\[
\sqrt{2}=\sup \iota(S).
\]
Thus the bounded-above rational set with no rational supremum has a supremum
in $\mathbb{R}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let
   > \[
   > S=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:0_{\mathbb{Q}}<q\land q\cdot q<2_{\mathbb{Q}}\}.
   > \]
   > Then
   > \[
   > \sqrt{2}=\sup \iota(S).
   > \]
   > Thus the bounded-above rational set with no rational supremum has a supremum
   > in $\mathbb{R}$.

items.title: Extended Real Addition Is Well Defined
items.statement:
For every pair $(x,y)$ in the domain of extended real addition, there is a
unique element $z\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
\[
z=x+y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every pair $(x,y)$ in the domain of extended real addition, there is a
   > unique element $z\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
   > \[
   > z=x+y.
   > \]

items.title: Extended Addition Extends Real Addition
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
x+_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}y=x+_{\mathbb{R}}y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > x+_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}y=x+_{\mathbb{R}}y.
   > \]

items.title: Addition with Infinities
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
x+(+\infty)=+\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
x+(-\infty)=-\infty.
\]
Moreover,
\[
(+\infty)+(+\infty)=+\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
(-\infty)+(-\infty)=-\infty.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > x+(+\infty)=+\infty
   > \quad\text{and}\quad
   > x+(-\infty)=-\infty.
   > \]
   > Moreover,
   > \[
   > (+\infty)+(+\infty)=+\infty
   > \quad\text{and}\quad
   > (-\infty)+(-\infty)=-\infty.
   > \]

items.title: Extended Real Negation Is Well Defined
items.statement:
For every $x\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$, there is a unique
$y\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
\[
y=-x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$, there is a unique
   > $y\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
   > \[
   > y=-x.
   > \]

items.title: Extended Real Multiplication Is Well Defined
items.statement:
For every pair $(x,y)$ in the domain of extended real multiplication, there is
a unique element $z\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
\[
z=xy.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every pair $(x,y)$ in the domain of extended real multiplication, there is
   > a unique element $z\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
   > \[
   > z=xy.
   > \]

items.title: Extended Multiplication Extends Real Multiplication
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
x\cdot_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}y=x\cdot_{\mathbb{R}}y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > x\cdot_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}y=x\cdot_{\mathbb{R}}y.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication with Infinities
items.statement:
If $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $x>0$, then
\[
x(+\infty)=+\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
x(-\infty)=-\infty.
\]
If $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $x<0$, then
\[
x(+\infty)=-\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
x(-\infty)=+\infty.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $x>0$, then
   > \[
   > x(+\infty)=+\infty
   > \quad\text{and}\quad
   > x(-\infty)=-\infty.
   > \]
   > If $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $x<0$, then
   > \[
   > x(+\infty)=-\infty
   > \quad\text{and}\quad
   > x(-\infty)=+\infty.
   > \]

items.title: Indeterminate Extended Real Forms
items.statement:
The expressions
\[
(+\infty)+(-\infty),\qquad
(-\infty)+(+\infty),\qquad
0\cdot(+\infty),\qquad
0\cdot(-\infty)
\]
are not defined in the extended real arithmetic introduced here.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The expressions
   > \[
   > (+\infty)+(-\infty),\qquad
   > (-\infty)+(+\infty),\qquad
   > 0\cdot(+\infty),\qquad
   > 0\cdot(-\infty)
   > \]
   > are not defined in the extended real arithmetic introduced here.

items.title: Real Rays as Extended Intervals
items.statement:
For $a\in\mathbb{R}$, the real rays
\[
(a,+\infty),\qquad [a,+\infty),\qquad
(-\infty,a),\qquad (-\infty,a]
\]
are the finite parts of extended intervals with infinite endpoints.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For $a\in\mathbb{R}$, the real rays
   > \[
   > (a,+\infty),\qquad [a,+\infty),\qquad
   > (-\infty,a),\qquad (-\infty,a]
   > \]
   > are the finite parts of extended intervals with infinite endpoints.

items.title: Extended Closed Rays Contain Infinite Endpoints
items.statement:
For $a\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
+\infty\in [a,+\infty]_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
-\infty\in [-\infty,a]_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For $a\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > +\infty\in [a,+\infty]_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}
   > \quad\text{and}\quad
   > -\infty\in [-\infty,a]_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}.
   > \]

items.title: Comparison with Infinities
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
-\infty<x<+\infty.
\]
Also,
\[
-\infty\le y\le+\infty
\]
for every $y\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > -\infty<x<+\infty.
   > \]
   > Also,
   > \[
   > -\infty\le y\le+\infty
   > \]
   > for every $y\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$.

items.title: The Extended Real Line Is Closed and Bounded
items.statement:
In $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$,
\[
\overline{\mathbb{R}}=[-\infty,+\infty].
\]
Thus the whole extended real line has both a least element and a greatest
element.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > In $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$,
   > \[
   > \overline{\mathbb{R}}=[-\infty,+\infty].
   > \]
   > Thus the whole extended real line has both a least element and a greatest
   > element.

items.title: Extended Interval Order Characterization
items.statement:
A subset $I\subseteq\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ is an extended real interval if and
only if for all $x,z\in I$ with $x\le z$,
\[
[x,z]_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}\subseteq I.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > A subset $I\subseteq\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ is an extended real interval if and
   > only if for all $x,z\in I$ with $x\le z$,
   > \[
   > [x,z]_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}\subseteq I.
   > \]

items.title: Extended Real Order Is Well Defined
items.statement:
The relation $\le_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}$ defines a binary relation on
$\overline{\mathbb{R}}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The relation $\le_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}$ defines a binary relation on
   > $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$.

items.title: Extended Real Order Is Total
items.statement:
The ordered set $(\overline{\mathbb{R}},\le_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}})$ is a
totally ordered set.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The ordered set $(\overline{\mathbb{R}},\le_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}})$ is a
   > totally ordered set.

items.title: Real Order Embeds in the Extended Real Order
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
x\le_{\mathbb{R}}y
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\le_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > x\le_{\mathbb{R}}y
   > \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
   > x\le_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}y.
   > \]

items.title: Complex Coordinate Equivalence Is Reflexive
items.statement:
For every $(a,b)\in\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{C}$,
\[
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(a,b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $(a,b)\in\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{C}$,
   > \[
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(a,b).
   > \]

items.title: Complex Coordinate Equivalence Is Symmetric
items.statement:
For all prepairs $(a,b),(c,d)$,
\[
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(c,d)
\Longrightarrow
(c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(a,b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all prepairs $(a,b),(c,d)$,
   > \[
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(c,d)
   > \Longrightarrow
   > (c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(a,b).
   > \]

items.title: Complex Coordinate Equivalence Is Transitive
items.statement:
For all prepairs $(a,b),(c,d),(e,f)$,
\[
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(c,d)\land
(c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(e,f)
\Longrightarrow
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(e,f).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all prepairs $(a,b),(c,d),(e,f)$,
   > \[
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(c,d)\land
   > (c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(e,f)
   > \Longrightarrow
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(e,f).
   > \]

items.title: Complex Coordinate Equivalence Is an Equivalence Relation
items.statement:
The relation $\sim_{\mathbb{C}}$ is an equivalence relation on
\(\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{C}\).
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The relation $\sim_{\mathbb{C}}$ is an equivalence relation on
   > \(\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{C}\).
