   > Then
   > \[
   > U+W=U\oplus W
   > \]
   > if and only if
   > \[
   > U \cap W = \{0\}.
   > \]

items.title: Characterizations of Order-Isomorphisms for Finite Posets
items.statement:
Let $(P, \leq_P)$ and $(Q, \leq_Q)$ be finite partially ordered sets and
let $\varphi : P \to Q$ be a bijection. The following are equivalent:
- $\varphi$ is an order-isomorphism.
- For all $x, y \in P$:\; $x <_P y \;\Longleftrightarrow\; \varphi(x) <_Q \varphi(y)$.
- For all $x, y \in P$:\; $x \prec_P y \;\Longleftrightarrow\; \varphi(x) \prec_Q \varphi(y)$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(P, \leq_P)$ and $(Q, \leq_Q)$ be finite partially ordered sets and
   > let $\varphi : P \to Q$ be a bijection. The following are equivalent:
   > - $\varphi$ is an order-isomorphism.
   > - For all $x, y \in P$:\; $x <_P y \;\Longleftrightarrow\; \varphi(x) <_Q \varphi(y)$.
   > - For all $x, y \in P$:\; $x \prec_P y \;\Longleftrightarrow\; \varphi(x) \prec_Q \varphi(y)$.

items.title: Hasse Diagram Characterization for Finite Posets
items.statement:
Let $(P, \leq_P)$ and $(Q, \leq_Q)$ be finite partially ordered sets.
Then $P$ and $Q$ are order-isomorphic if and only if their Hasse diagrams
are isomorphic as directed graphs --- that is, identical up to relabeling
of elements.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(P, \leq_P)$ and $(Q, \leq_Q)$ be finite partially ordered sets.
   > Then $P$ and $Q$ are order-isomorphic if and only if their Hasse diagrams
   > are isomorphic as directed graphs --- that is, identical up to relabeling
   > of elements.

items.title: Duality Principle
items.statement:
Let $\Phi$ be a statement about partially ordered sets, expressed purely
in terms of $\leq$, that holds in every partially ordered set. Then the
dual statement $\Phi^{\mathrm{op}}$, obtained by replacing every
occurrence of $\leq$ with $\geq$, also holds in every partially ordered
set.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $\Phi$ be a statement about partially ordered sets, expressed purely
   > in terms of $\leq$, that holds in every partially ordered set. Then the
   > dual statement $\Phi^{\mathrm{op}}$, obtained by replacing every
   > occurrence of $\leq$ with $\geq$, also holds in every partially ordered
   > set.

items.title: Every Nonempty Finite Poset Has a Maximal Element
items.statement:
Let $(P, \leq)$ be a finite partially ordered set. Then every nonempty
subset $Q \subseteq P$ has at least one maximal element. Furthermore,
for every $x \in P$ there exists $y \in \operatorname{Max}(P)$ with
$x \leq y$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(P, \leq)$ be a finite partially ordered set. Then every nonempty
   > subset $Q \subseteq P$ has at least one maximal element. Furthermore,
   > for every $x \in P$ there exists $y \in \operatorname{Max}(P)$ with
   > $x \leq y$.

items.title: Predicates and Power Sets Are Order-Isomorphic
items.statement:
The map $\Phi : (\mathcal{P}^*(X), \leq) \to (\mathcal{P}(X), \subseteq)$
is an \hyperref[def:order-isomorphism]{order-isomorphism}.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The map $\Phi : (\mathcal{P}^*(X), \leq) \to (\mathcal{P}(X), \subseteq)$
   > is an \hyperref[def:order-isomorphism]{order-isomorphism}.

items.title: Every Order-Embedding Is Injective
items.statement:
Let $(P, \leq_P)$ and $(Q, \leq_Q)$ be partially ordered sets, and let
$\varphi : P \to Q$ be an order-embedding. Then $\varphi$ is injective.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(P, \leq_P)$ and $(Q, \leq_Q)$ be partially ordered sets, and let
   > $\varphi : P \to Q$ be an order-embedding. Then $\varphi$ is injective.

items.title: Convex hull as the smallest convex set
items.statement:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2\). Then \(\conv(P)\) is convex, contains \(P\), and
is contained in every convex set that contains \(P\). Hence
\[
 \conv(P)
 =
 \bigcap\{K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2 : K\text{ is convex and }P\subseteq K\}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2\). Then \(\conv(P)\) is convex, contains \(P\), and
   > is contained in every convex set that contains \(P\). Hence
   > \[
   >  \conv(P)
   >  =
   >  \bigcap\{K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2 : K\text{ is convex and }P\subseteq K\}.
   > \]

items.title: Supporting functional characterization of hull vertices
items.statement:
Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) be finite and in general position. A point \(p\in P\)
is a vertex of \(\conv(P)\) if and only if there exists a direction
\(d\in\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}\) such that
\[
 \langle d,p\rangle>\langle d,q\rangle
 \qquad
 \text{for all } q\in P\setminus\{p\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(p\) is the unique point of \(P\) attaining
\[
 \max_{q\in P}\langle d,q\rangle.
\]
Thus every hull vertex is a maximum of \(P\) under some linear functional.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) be finite and in general position. A point \(p\in P\)
   > is a vertex of \(\conv(P)\) if and only if there exists a direction
   > \(d\in\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}\) such that
   > \[
   >  \langle d,p\rangle>\langle d,q\rangle
   >  \qquad
   >  \text{for all } q\in P\setminus\{p\}.
   > \]
   > Equivalently, \(p\) is the unique point of \(P\) attaining
   > \[
   >  \max_{q\in P}\langle d,q\rangle.
   > \]
   > Thus every hull vertex is a maximum of \(P\) under some linear functional.

items.title: Monotone slope characterization of the upper hull
items.statement:
Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) be finite and in general position. Let
\[
 v_0,v_1,\dots,v_m
\]
be the vertices of the upper hull of \(P\), listed in increasing
\(x\)-coordinate, and define
\[
 s_k
 =
 \frac{y(v_{k+1})-y(v_k)}{x(v_{k+1})-x(v_k)},
 \qquad
 k=0,1,\dots,m-1.
\]
Then
\[
 s_0>s_1>\cdots>s_{m-1}.
\]
Conversely, if points \(w_0,\dots,w_m\) satisfy
\[
 x(w_0)<x(w_1)<\cdots<x(w_m)
\]
and their consecutive slopes are strictly decreasing, then every \(w_k\) is a
vertex of
\[
 \conv(\{w_0,\dots,w_m\}).
\]
The lower hull is characterized similarly, with strictly increasing consecutive
slopes.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) be finite and in general position. Let
   > \[
   >  v_0,v_1,\dots,v_m
   > \]
   > be the vertices of the upper hull of \(P\), listed in increasing
   > \(x\)-coordinate, and define
   > \[
   >  s_k
   >  =
   >  \frac{y(v_{k+1})-y(v_k)}{x(v_{k+1})-x(v_k)},
   >  \qquad
   >  k=0,1,\dots,m-1.
   > \]
   > Then
   > \[
   >  s_0>s_1>\cdots>s_{m-1}.
   > \]
   > Conversely, if points \(w_0,\dots,w_m\) satisfy
   > \[
   >  x(w_0)<x(w_1)<\cdots<x(w_m)
   > \]
   > and their consecutive slopes are strictly decreasing, then every \(w_k\) is a
   > vertex of
   > \[
   >  \conv(\{w_0,\dots,w_m\}).
   > \]
   > The lower hull is characterized similarly, with strictly increasing consecutive
   > slopes.

items.title: Greedy slope construction of the upper hull
items.statement:
Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) be finite and in general position. Define
\[
 v_0=\argmin_{p\in P}x(p).
\]
Given \(v_k\) with
\[
 x(v_k)<\max_{p\in P}x(p),
\]
define
\[
 v_{k+1}
 =
 \argmax_{\substack{q\in P\\x(q)>x(v_k)}}
 \frac{y(q)-y(v_k)}{x(q)-x(v_k)}.
\]
Terminate once
\[
 v_k=\argmax_{p\in P}x(p).
\]
Then the points
\[
 v_0,v_1,\dots,v_m
\]
produced by this construction are exactly the vertices of the upper hull of
\(P\), and the slopes encountered along the way are strictly decreasing.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^2\) be finite and in general position. Define
   > \[
   >  v_0=\argmin_{p\in P}x(p).
   > \]
   > Given \(v_k\) with
   > \[
   >  x(v_k)<\max_{p\in P}x(p),
   > \]
   > define
   > \[
   >  v_{k+1}
   >  =
   >  \argmax_{\substack{q\in P\\x(q)>x(v_k)}}
   >  \frac{y(q)-y(v_k)}{x(q)-x(v_k)}.
   > \]
   > Terminate once
   > \[
   >  v_k=\argmax_{p\in P}x(p).
   > \]
   > Then the points
   > \[
   >  v_0,v_1,\dots,v_m
   > \]
   > produced by this construction are exactly the vertices of the upper hull of
   > \(P\), and the slopes encountered along the way are strictly decreasing.

items.title: Logical Equivalence is an Equivalence Relation
items.statement:
Logical equivalence is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive on \(\WFF\):
\[
\varphi\equiv\varphi,
\qquad
\varphi\equiv\psi\Longrightarrow\psi\equiv\varphi,
\]
and
\[
(\varphi\equiv\psi\land\psi\equiv\chi)
\Longrightarrow
\varphi\equiv\chi.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Logical equivalence is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive on \(\WFF\):
   > \[
   > \varphi\equiv\varphi,
   > \qquad
   > \varphi\equiv\psi\Longrightarrow\psi\equiv\varphi,
   > \]
   > and
   > \[
   > (\varphi\equiv\psi\land\psi\equiv\chi)
   > \Longrightarrow
   > \varphi\equiv\chi.
   > \]

items.title: Structural Induction for Propositional Formulas
Structural Recursion for Propositional Formulas
Constructor Disjointness for Propositional Formulas
Constructor Injectivity for Propositional Formulas
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The propositional formula constructors are injective:
   > - if \(\neg\varphi=\neg\psi\), then \(\varphi=\psi\);
   > - if \((\varphi\circ\psi)=(\alpha\star\beta)\), then \(\varphi=\alpha\), \(\psi=\beta\), and \(\circ=\star\).

items.title: Unique Decomposition for Propositional Formulas
Unique Extension of a Truth Assignment
items.statement:
Every truth assignment
\[
v:\Prop\to\mathbb{B}
\]
has a unique extension
\[
\widehat v:\WFF\to\mathbb{B}
\]
satisfying the recursive truth clauses for propositional variables and the
primitive connectives.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every truth assignment
   > \[
   > v:\Prop\to\mathbb{B}
   > \]
   > has a unique extension
   > \[
   > \widehat v:\WFF\to\mathbb{B}
   > \]
   > satisfying the recursive truth clauses for propositional variables and the
   > primitive connectives.

items.title: Basic Boolean Equivalence Laws
items.statement:
For all formulas \(\varphi,\psi,\chi\in\WFF\), the following logical equivalences hold.

Commutativity:
\[
\varphi\land\psi\equiv\psi\land\varphi,
\qquad
\varphi\lor\psi\equiv\psi\lor\varphi.
\]

Associativity:
\[
(\varphi\land\psi)\land\chi
\equiv
\varphi\land(\psi\land\chi),
\qquad
(\varphi\lor\psi)\lor\chi
\equiv
\varphi\lor(\psi\lor\chi).
\]

Idempotence:
\[
\varphi\land\varphi\equiv\varphi,
\qquad
\varphi\lor\varphi\equiv\varphi.
\]

Double negation:
\[
\neg\neg\varphi\equiv\varphi.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all formulas \(\varphi,\psi,\chi\in\WFF\), the following logical equivalences hold.
   >
   > Commutativity:
   > \[
   > \varphi\land\psi\equiv\psi\land\varphi,
   > \qquad
   > \varphi\lor\psi\equiv\psi\lor\varphi.
   > \]
   >
   > Associativity:
   > \[
   > (\varphi\land\psi)\land\chi
   > \equiv
   > \varphi\land(\psi\land\chi),
   > \qquad
   > (\varphi\lor\psi)\lor\chi
   > \equiv
   > \varphi\lor(\psi\lor\chi).
   > \]
   >
   > Idempotence:
   > \[
   > \varphi\land\varphi\equiv\varphi,
   > \qquad
   > \varphi\lor\varphi\equiv\varphi.
   > \]
   >
   > Double negation:
   > \[
   > \neg\neg\varphi\equiv\varphi.
   > \]

items.title: Identity and Domination Laws
items.statement:
Let \(\top\) be any tautological formula and let \(\bot\) be any contradictory formula. Then for every \(\varphi\in\WFF\):
\[
\varphi\land\top\equiv\varphi,
\qquad
\varphi\lor\bot\equiv\varphi,
\]
and
\[
\varphi\land\bot\equiv\bot,
\qquad
\varphi\lor\top\equiv\top.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let \(\top\) be any tautological formula and let \(\bot\) be any contradictory formula. Then for every \(\varphi\in\WFF\):
   > \[
   > \varphi\land\top\equiv\varphi,
   > \qquad
   > \varphi\lor\bot\equiv\varphi,
   > \]
   > and
   > \[
   > \varphi\land\bot\equiv\bot,
   > \qquad
   > \varphi\lor\top\equiv\top.
   > \]

items.title: De Morgan Laws for Propositional Logic
items.statement:
For all \(\varphi,\psi\in\WFF\),
\[
\neg(\varphi\land\psi)
\equiv
\neg\varphi\lor\neg\psi,
\]
and
\[
\neg(\varphi\lor\psi)
\equiv
\neg\varphi\land\neg\psi.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all \(\varphi,\psi\in\WFF\),
   > \[
   > \neg(\varphi\land\psi)
   > \equiv
   > \neg\varphi\lor\neg\psi,
   > \]
   > and
   > \[
   > \neg(\varphi\lor\psi)
   > \equiv
   > \neg\varphi\land\neg\psi.
   > \]

items.title: Distributive Laws for Propositional Logic
items.statement:
For all \(\varphi,\psi,\chi\in\WFF\),
\[
\varphi\land(\psi\lor\chi)
\equiv
(\varphi\land\psi)\lor(\varphi\land\chi),
\]
and
\[
\varphi\lor(\psi\land\chi)
\equiv
(\varphi\lor\psi)\land(\varphi\lor\chi).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all \(\varphi,\psi,\chi\in\WFF\),
   > \[
   > \varphi\land(\psi\lor\chi)
   > \equiv
   > (\varphi\land\psi)\lor(\varphi\land\chi),
   > \]
   > and
   > \[
   > \varphi\lor(\psi\land\chi)
   > \equiv
   > (\varphi\lor\psi)\land(\varphi\lor\chi).
   > \]

items.title: Absorption Laws
items.statement:
For all \(\varphi,\psi\in\WFF\),
\[
\varphi\land(\varphi\lor\psi)\equiv\varphi,
\]
and
\[
\varphi\lor(\varphi\land\psi)\equiv\varphi.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all \(\varphi,\psi\in\WFF\),
   > \[
   > \varphi\land(\varphi\lor\psi)\equiv\varphi,
   > \]
   > and
   > \[
   > \varphi\lor(\varphi\land\psi)\equiv\varphi.
   > \]

items.title: Conditional Equivalence Laws
items.statement:
For all \(\varphi,\psi\in\WFF\),
\[
\varphi\to\psi
\equiv
\neg\varphi\lor\psi,
\]
and
\[
\neg(\varphi\to\psi)
\equiv
\varphi\land\neg\psi.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all \(\varphi,\psi\in\WFF\),
   > \[
   > \varphi\to\psi
   > \equiv
   > \neg\varphi\lor\psi,
   > \]
   > and
   > \[
   > \neg(\varphi\to\psi)
   > \equiv
   > \varphi\land\neg\psi.
   > \]

items.title: Biconditional Equivalence Laws
items.statement:
For all \(\varphi,\psi\in\WFF\),
\[
\varphi\leftrightarrow\psi
\equiv
(\varphi\to\psi)\land(\psi\to\varphi),
\]
and
\[
\varphi\leftrightarrow\psi
\equiv
(\varphi\land\psi)\lor(\neg\varphi\land\neg\psi).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all \(\varphi,\psi\in\WFF\),
   > \[
   > \varphi\leftrightarrow\psi
   > \equiv
   > (\varphi\to\psi)\land(\psi\to\varphi),
   > \]
   > and
   > \[
   > \varphi\leftrightarrow\psi
   > \equiv
   > (\varphi\land\psi)\lor(\neg\varphi\land\neg\psi).
   > \]

items.title: Coincidence Lemma for Propositional Logic
items.statement:
Let \(v,w:\Prop\to\mathbb{B}\) be truth assignments. If \(v\) and \(w\) agree on every propositional variable occurring in \(\varphi\), then they assign the same truth value to \(\varphi\):
\[
v|_{\operatorname{Var}(\varphi)}
=
w|_{\operatorname{Var}(\varphi)}
\Longrightarrow
\widehat v(\varphi)=\widehat w(\varphi).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let \(v,w:\Prop\to\mathbb{B}\) be truth assignments. If \(v\) and \(w\) agree on every propositional variable occurring in \(\varphi\), then they assign the same truth value to \(\varphi\):
   > \[
   > v|_{\operatorname{Var}(\varphi)}
   > =
   > w|_{\operatorname{Var}(\varphi)}
   > \Longrightarrow
   > \widehat v(\varphi)=\widehat w(\varphi).
   > \]

items.title: Replacement of Logical Equivalents
items.statement:
Replacing logically equivalent formulas inside a formula context preserves logical equivalence:
\[
\varphi\equiv\psi
\Longrightarrow
C[\varphi]\equiv C[\psi].
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Replacing logically equivalent formulas inside a formula context preserves logical equivalence:
   > \[
   > \varphi\equiv\psi
   > \Longrightarrow
   > C[\varphi]\equiv C[\psi].
   > \]

items.title: Finiteness of Variables in a Formula
items.statement: For every \(\varphi\in\WFF\), the set \(\operatorname{Var}(\varphi)\) is finite.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every \(\varphi\in\WFF\), the set \(\operatorname{Var}(\varphi)\) is finite.

items.title: Finite Truth-Table Theorem
items.statement: Every propositional formula has a finite truth table. More precisely, if \(\operatorname{Var}(\varphi)\) has \(n\) elements, then \(\varphi\) has a truth table with \(2^n\) rows.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every propositional formula has a finite truth table. More precisely, if \(\operatorname{Var}(\varphi)\) has \(n\) elements, then \(\varphi\) has a truth table with \(2^n\) rows.

items.title: Truth-Table Validity Test for Argument Forms
items.statement:
An argument form \((\Gamma,\varphi)\) is valid if and only if no row of its truth
table makes every formula in \(\Gamma\) true and \(\varphi\) false.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > An argument form \((\Gamma,\varphi)\) is valid if and only if no row of its truth
   > table makes every formula in \(\Gamma\) true and \(\varphi\) false.

items.title: Affirming the Consequent is Invalid
items.statement:
The argument form
\[
\varphi\to\psi,\qquad \psi \quad\therefore\quad \varphi
\]
is invalid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The argument form
   > \[
   > \varphi\to\psi,\qquad \psi \quad\therefore\quad \varphi
   > \]
   > is invalid.

items.title: Denying the Antecedent is Invalid
items.statement:
The argument form
\[
\varphi\to\psi,\qquad \neg\varphi \quad\therefore\quad \neg\psi
\]
is invalid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The argument form
   > \[
   > \varphi\to\psi,\qquad \neg\varphi \quad\therefore\quad \neg\psi
   > \]
   > is invalid.

items.title: Replacement Rules Preserve Logical Equivalence
items.statement:
If a formula \(\psi\) is obtained from a formula \(\varphi\) by finitely many
applications of rules of replacement, then \(\varphi\equiv\psi\).
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If a formula \(\psi\) is obtained from a formula \(\varphi\) by finitely many
   > applications of rules of replacement, then \(\varphi\equiv\psi\).

items.title: Tautological Implication Gives a Valid Argument Form
items.statement:
Let \(\Gamma=\{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n\}\subseteq\WFF\) and let
\(\varphi\in\WFF\). If
\[
(\gamma_1\land\cdots\land\gamma_n)\to\varphi
\]
is a tautology, then the argument form \((\Gamma,\varphi)\) is valid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let \(\Gamma=\{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n\}\subseteq\WFF\) and let
   > \(\varphi\in\WFF\). If
   > \[
   > (\gamma_1\land\cdots\land\gamma_n)\to\varphi
   > \]
   > is a tautology, then the argument form \((\Gamma,\varphi)\) is valid.

items.title: Modus Ponens is Valid
items.statement:
The argument form
\[
\varphi,\qquad \varphi\to\psi \quad\therefore\quad \psi
\]
is valid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The argument form
   > \[
   > \varphi,\qquad \varphi\to\psi \quad\therefore\quad \psi
   > \]
   > is valid.

items.title: Modus Tollens is Valid
items.statement:
The argument form
\[
\varphi\to\psi,\qquad \neg\psi \quad\therefore\quad \neg\varphi
\]
is valid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The argument form
   > \[
   > \varphi\to\psi,\qquad \neg\psi \quad\therefore\quad \neg\varphi
   > \]
   > is valid.

items.title: Hypothetical Syllogism is Valid
items.statement:
The argument form
\[
\varphi\to\psi,\qquad \psi\to\chi \quad\therefore\quad \varphi\to\chi
\]
is valid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The argument form
   > \[
   > \varphi\to\psi,\qquad \psi\to\chi \quad\therefore\quad \varphi\to\chi
   > \]
   > is valid.

items.title: Disjunctive Syllogism is Valid
items.statement:
The argument form
\[
\varphi\lor\psi,\qquad \neg\varphi \quad\therefore\quad \psi
\]
is valid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The argument form
   > \[
   > \varphi\lor\psi,\qquad \neg\varphi \quad\therefore\quad \psi
   > \]
   > is valid.

items.title: Addition is Valid
items.statement:
The argument form
\[
\varphi \quad\therefore\quad \varphi\lor\psi
\]
is valid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The argument form
   > \[
   > \varphi \quad\therefore\quad \varphi\lor\psi
   > \]
   > is valid.

items.title: Simplification is Valid
items.statement:
The argument form
\[
\varphi\land\psi \quad\therefore\quad \varphi
\]
is valid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The argument form
   > \[
   > \varphi\land\psi \quad\therefore\quad \varphi
   > \]
   > is valid.

items.title: Conjunction Introduction is Valid
items.statement:
The argument form
\[
\varphi,\qquad \psi \quad\therefore\quad \varphi\land\psi
\]
is valid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The argument form
   > \[
   > \varphi,\qquad \psi \quad\therefore\quad \varphi\land\psi
   > \]
   > is valid.

items.title: Constructive Dilemma is Valid
items.statement:
The argument form
\[
\varphi\to\chi,\qquad \psi\to\theta,\qquad \varphi\lor\psi
\quad\therefore\quad
\chi\lor\theta
\]
is valid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The argument form
   > \[
   > \varphi\to\chi,\qquad \psi\to\theta,\qquad \varphi\lor\psi
   > \quad\therefore\quad
   > \chi\lor\theta
   > \]
   > is valid.

items.title: Destructive Dilemma is Valid
items.statement:
The argument form
\[
\varphi\to\chi,\qquad \psi\to\theta,\qquad \neg\chi\lor\neg\theta
\quad\therefore\quad
\neg\varphi\lor\neg\psi
\]
is valid.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The argument form
   > \[
   > \varphi\to\chi,\qquad \psi\to\theta,\qquad \neg\chi\lor\neg\theta
   > \quad\therefore\quad
   > \neg\varphi\lor\neg\psi
   > \]
   > is valid.

items.title: Finite Unsatisfiability Witness
items.statement:
Let \(\Gamma\subseteq\WFF\). If there exists a finite
\(\Delta\subseteq\Gamma\) such that \(\Delta\) is unsatisfiable, then
\(\Gamma\) is unsatisfiable.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let \(\Gamma\subseteq\WFF\). If there exists a finite
   > \(\Delta\subseteq\Gamma\) such that \(\Delta\) is unsatisfiable, then
   > \(\Gamma\) is unsatisfiable.

items.title: Finite Witness Contrapositive
items.statement:
Let \(\Gamma\subseteq\WFF\). If \(\Gamma\) is satisfiable, then every finite
subset of \(\Gamma\) is satisfiable.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let \(\Gamma\subseteq\WFF\). If \(\Gamma\) is satisfiable, then every finite
   > subset of \(\Gamma\) is satisfiable.

items.title: Propositional Compactness
items.statement:
Let \(\Gamma\subseteq\WFF\). If every finite subset of \(\Gamma\) is
satisfiable, then \(\Gamma\) is satisfiable.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let \(\Gamma\subseteq\WFF\). If every finite subset of \(\Gamma\) is
   > satisfiable, then \(\Gamma\) is satisfiable.

items.title: DNF Representation of Boolean Functions
items.statement:
Every Boolean function \(f:\mathbb{B}^n\to\mathbb{B}\) is represented by a
formula in disjunctive normal form using variables \(P_1,\ldots,P_n\).
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every Boolean function \(f:\mathbb{B}^n\to\mathbb{B}\) is represented by a
   > formula in disjunctive normal form using variables \(P_1,\ldots,P_n\).

items.title: Conjunction and Disjunction are not Functionally Complete
items.statement: The connective basis \(\{\land,\lor\}\) is not functionally complete.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The connective basis \(\{\land,\lor\}\) is not functionally complete.

items.title: Standard Connectives are Functionally Complete
items.statement:
The connective basis
\[
\{\neg,\land,\lor\}
\]
is functionally complete.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The connective basis
   > \[
   > \{\neg,\land,\lor\}
   > \]
   > is functionally complete.

items.title: Negation and Conjunction are Functionally Complete
items.statement:
The connective basis
\[
\{\neg,\land\}
\]
is functionally complete.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The connective basis
   > \[
   > \{\neg,\land\}
   > \]
   > is functionally complete.

items.title: NAND is Functionally Complete
items.statement: The one-connective basis \(\{\uparrow\}\) is functionally complete.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The one-connective basis \(\{\uparrow\}\) is functionally complete.

items.title: Negation and Disjunction are Functionally Complete
items.statement:
The connective basis
\[
\{\neg,\lor\}
\]
is functionally complete.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The connective basis
   > \[
   > \{\neg,\lor\}
   > \]
   > is functionally complete.

items.title: NOR is Functionally Complete
items.statement: The one-connective basis \(\{\downarrow\}\) is functionally complete.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The one-connective basis \(\{\downarrow\}\) is functionally complete.

items.title: NAND and NOR are Minimal Complete Bases
items.statement:
The one-connective bases \(\{\uparrow\}\) and \(\{\downarrow\}\) are minimal
complete bases.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The one-connective bases \(\{\uparrow\}\) and \(\{\downarrow\}\) are minimal
   > complete bases.

items.title: Existence of Negation Normal Form

For every formula \(\varphi\in\WFF\), there exists a formula \(\psi\in\WFF\)

\[

\]

   > such that \(\psi\) is in negation normal form and
   > \[
   > \varphi\equiv\psi.
   > \]

items.statement:
Normal forms give finite certificates for semantic classification. For any

items.markdown:

   > Normal forms give finite certificates for semantic classification. For any
