is a Dedekind cut.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ is nonempty and bounded above, then
   > \[
   > \bigcup_{\alpha\in S}\alpha
   > \]
   > is a Dedekind cut.

items.title: Least-Upper-Bound Property
items.statement:
Every nonempty subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ that is bounded above has a least
upper bound, namely
\[
\sup S=\bigcup_{\alpha\in S}\alpha.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every nonempty subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ that is bounded above has a least
   > upper bound, namely
   > \[
   > \sup S=\bigcup_{\alpha\in S}\alpha.
   > \]

items.title: Zero Is Not One in $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
In $\mathbb{R}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{R}}\ne 1_{\mathbb{R}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > In $\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{R}}\ne 1_{\mathbb{R}}.
   > \]

items.title: Product of Nonnegative Cuts Is a Cut
items.statement: If $\alpha,\beta\ge 0_{\mathbb{R}}$, then $\alpha\cdot\beta$ is a Dedekind cut.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $\alpha,\beta\ge 0_{\mathbb{R}}$, then $\alpha\cdot\beta$ is a Dedekind cut.

items.title: Product of Cuts Is a Cut
items.statement: If $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\alpha\cdot\beta\in\mathbb{R}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\alpha\cdot\beta\in\mathbb{R}$.

items.title: Multiplication on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Associative
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
(\alpha\cdot\beta)\cdot\gamma=\alpha\cdot(\beta\cdot\gamma).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > (\alpha\cdot\beta)\cdot\gamma=\alpha\cdot(\beta\cdot\gamma).
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Commutative
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\cdot\beta=\beta\cdot\alpha.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\cdot\beta=\beta\cdot\alpha.
   > \]

items.title: One Is a Multiplicative Identity on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\cdot 1_{\mathbb{R}}=\alpha.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\cdot 1_{\mathbb{R}}=\alpha.
   > \]

items.title: Reciprocal of a Nonzero Cut Is a Cut
items.statement:
If $\alpha\ne0_{\mathbb{R}}$, then $\alpha^
{-1}\in\mathbb{R}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $\alpha\ne0_{\mathbb{R}}$, then $\alpha^
   > {-1}\in\mathbb{R}$.

items.title: Reciprocal Is a Multiplicative Inverse on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
If $\alpha\ne0_{\mathbb{R}}$, then
\[
\alpha\cdot\alpha^{-1}=1_{\mathbb{R}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $\alpha\ne0_{\mathbb{R}}$, then
   > \[
   > \alpha\cdot\alpha^{-1}=1_{\mathbb{R}}.
   > \]

items.title: Nonzero $\mathbb{R}$ Is a Multiplicative Abelian Group
items.statement:
The structure $(\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0_{\mathbb{R}}\},\cdot,1_{\mathbb{R}})$
is an abelian group.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The structure $(\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0_{\mathbb{R}}\},\cdot,1_{\mathbb{R}})$
   > is an abelian group.

items.title: Distributivity on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\cdot(\beta+\gamma)=\alpha\cdot\beta+\alpha\cdot\gamma.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\cdot(\beta+\gamma)=\alpha\cdot\beta+\alpha\cdot\gamma.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Is a Field
items.statement: The structure $(\mathbb{R},+,\cdot,0_{\mathbb{R}},1_{\mathbb{R}})$ is a field.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The structure $(\mathbb{R},+,\cdot,0_{\mathbb{R}},1_{\mathbb{R}})$ is a field.

items.title: Addition Preserves Order on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha<\beta \Longrightarrow \alpha+\gamma<\beta+\gamma,
\]
and the corresponding non-strict statement also holds.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha<\beta \Longrightarrow \alpha+\gamma<\beta+\gamma,
   > \]
   > and the corresponding non-strict statement also holds.

items.title: Multiplication by Positives Preserves Order on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{R}}<\gamma\land\alpha<\beta
\Longrightarrow
\gamma\cdot\alpha<\gamma\cdot\beta.
\]
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{R}}<\gamma\land\alpha<\beta
   > \Longrightarrow
   > \gamma\cdot\alpha<\gamma\cdot\beta.
   > \]

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Reflexive
items.statement: For every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, $\alpha\le\alpha$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, $\alpha\le\alpha$.

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Antisymmetric
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\le\beta\land\beta\le\alpha \Longrightarrow \alpha=\beta.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\le\beta\land\beta\le\alpha \Longrightarrow \alpha=\beta.
   > \]

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Transitive
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\le\beta\land\beta\le\gamma \Longrightarrow \alpha\le\gamma.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\le\beta\land\beta\le\gamma \Longrightarrow \alpha\le\gamma.
   > \]

items.title: Comparability of Cuts
items.statement:
For all cuts $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\subseteq\beta \lor \beta\subseteq\alpha.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all cuts $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\subseteq\beta \lor \beta\subseteq\alpha.
   > \]

items.title: Order on $\mathbb{R}$ Is Total
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha\le\beta\lor\beta\le\alpha.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha\le\beta\lor\beta\le\alpha.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Is a Totally Ordered Set
items.statement: The ordered pair $(\mathbb{R},\le)$ is a total order.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The ordered pair $(\mathbb{R},\le)$ is a total order.

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Is an Ordered Field
items.statement:
The structure $(\mathbb{R},+,\cdot,0_{\mathbb{R}},1_{\mathbb{R}},\le)$ is an
ordered field.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The structure $(\mathbb{R},+,\cdot,0_{\mathbb{R}},1_{\mathbb{R}},\le)$ is an
   > ordered field.

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Is a Complete Ordered Field
items.statement: The ordered field $\mathbb{R}$ satisfies the least-upper-bound property.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The ordered field $\mathbb{R}$ satisfies the least-upper-bound property.

items.title: Uniqueness of the Complete Ordered Field
items.statement: Any two complete ordered fields are isomorphic by a unique order-isomorphism.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Any two complete ordered fields are isomorphic by a unique order-isomorphism.

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Is the Real Numbers
items.statement:
The field $\mathbb{R}$ is determined up to unique order-isomorphism by being a
complete ordered field.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The field $\mathbb{R}$ is determined up to unique order-isomorphism by being a
   > complete ordered field.

items.title: Greatest-Lower-Bound Property
items.statement:
Every nonempty subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ that is bounded below has a
greatest lower bound.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every nonempty subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ that is bounded below has a
   > greatest lower bound.

items.title: Rational Cuts Are Cuts
items.statement: For every $q\in\mathbb{Q}$, the set $q^{\ast}$ is a Dedekind cut.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $q\in\mathbb{Q}$, the set $q^{\ast}$ is a Dedekind cut.

items.title: Zero and One Are Reals
items.statement: The cuts $0_{\mathbb{R}}$ and $1_{\mathbb{R}}$ are elements of $\mathbb{R}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The cuts $0_{\mathbb{R}}$ and $1_{\mathbb{R}}$ are elements of $\mathbb{R}$.

items.title: Embedding Preserves Zero and One
items.statement:
The embedding satisfies
\[
\iota(0_{\mathbb{Q}})=0_{\mathbb{R}}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\iota(1_{\mathbb{Q}})=1_{\mathbb{R}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The embedding satisfies
   > \[
   > \iota(0_{\mathbb{Q}})=0_{\mathbb{R}}
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > \iota(1_{\mathbb{Q}})=1_{\mathbb{R}}.
   > \]

items.title: Embedding $\mathbb{Q}$ into $\mathbb{R}$ Is Injective
items.statement:
For all $p,q\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
\iota(p)=\iota(q) \Longrightarrow p=q.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $p,q\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > \iota(p)=\iota(q) \Longrightarrow p=q.
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves Addition and Multiplication
items.statement:
For all $p,q\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
\iota(p+q)=\iota(p)+\iota(q)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\iota(p\cdot q)=\iota(p)\cdot\iota(q).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $p,q\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > \iota(p+q)=\iota(p)+\iota(q)
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > \iota(p\cdot q)=\iota(p)\cdot\iota(q).
   > \]

items.title: Embedding Preserves Order
items.statement:
For all $p,q\in\mathbb{Q}$,
\[
p\le q \Longleftrightarrow \iota(p)\le\iota(q).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $p,q\in\mathbb{Q}$,
   > \[
   > p\le q \Longleftrightarrow \iota(p)\le\iota(q).
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{Q}$ Embeds into $\mathbb{R}$ as an Ordered Field
items.statement: The map $\iota$ is an injective order-preserving field homomorphism.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The map $\iota$ is an injective order-preserving field homomorphism.

items.title: Density of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\alpha<\beta \Longrightarrow \exists q\in\mathbb{Q}\,(\alpha<\iota(q)<\beta).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \alpha<\beta \Longrightarrow \exists q\in\mathbb{Q}\,(\alpha<\iota(q)<\beta).
   > \]

items.title: Archimedean Property of $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
0_{\mathbb{R}}<\alpha
\Longrightarrow
\exists n\in\mathbb{N}\,(\beta<\iota(n)\cdot\alpha).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{R}}<\alpha
   > \Longrightarrow
   > \exists n\in\mathbb{N}\,(\beta<\iota(n)\cdot\alpha).
   > \]

items.title: Field Laws Hold on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
Every theorem proved generically for fields holds in $\mathbb{R}$, including
zero product, double negation, sign rules, cancellation, uniqueness of
inverses, inverse laws, and exponent laws.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every theorem proved generically for fields holds in $\mathbb{R}$, including
   > zero product, double negation, sign rules, cancellation, uniqueness of
   > inverses, inverse laws, and exponent laws.

items.title: Ordered-Field Laws Hold on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement: Every theorem proved generically for ordered fields holds in $\mathbb{R}$.
items.section_title: Field And Ordered Field Structure Of R
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every theorem proved generically for ordered fields holds in $\mathbb{R}$.

items.title: Triangle Inequality
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
|\alpha+\beta|\le |\alpha|+|\beta|.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > |\alpha+\beta|\le |\alpha|+|\beta|.
   > \]

items.title: Trichotomy on $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement:
For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, exactly one of
\[
\alpha<\beta,\qquad \alpha=\beta,\qquad \beta<\alpha
\]
holds.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, exactly one of
   > \[
   > \alpha<\beta,\qquad \alpha=\beta,\qquad \beta<\alpha
   > \]
   > holds.

items.title: Existence of Square Roots
items.statement:
For every real number $a\ge 0$, there exists $x\in\mathbb{R}$ such that
\[
x\ge 0
\quad\text{and}\quad
x^2=a.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every real number $a\ge 0$, there exists $x\in\mathbb{R}$ such that
   > \[
   > x\ge 0
   > \quad\text{and}\quad
   > x^2=a.
   > \]

items.title: Uniqueness of Nonnegative Square Roots
items.statement:
If $x,y\ge 0$ and
\[
x^2=y^2,
\]
then
\[
x=y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $x,y\ge 0$ and
   > \[
   > x^2=y^2,
   > \]
   > then
   > \[
   > x=y.
   > \]

items.title: The Square-Root-of-Two Cut Is a Cut
items.statement: The set $\sqrt{2}$ is a Dedekind cut.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The set $\sqrt{2}$ is a Dedekind cut.

items.title: Its Square Is Two
items.statement:
In $\mathbb{R}$,
\[
\sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}=2_{\mathbb{R}},
\]
where $2_{\mathbb{R}}:=\iota(2_{\mathbb{Q}})$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > In $\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > \sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{2}=2_{\mathbb{R}},
   > \]
   > where $2_{\mathbb{R}}:=\iota(2_{\mathbb{Q}})$.

items.title: Square Root of Two Is Irrational
items.statement:
\[
\sqrt2\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > \[
   > \sqrt2\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{R}$ Contains the Supremum $\mathbb{Q}$ Was Missing
items.statement:
Let
\[
S=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:0_{\mathbb{Q}}<q\land q\cdot q<2_{\mathbb{Q}}\}.
\]
Then
\[
\sqrt{2}=\sup \iota(S).
\]
Thus the bounded-above rational set with no rational supremum has a supremum
in $\mathbb{R}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let
   > \[
   > S=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:0_{\mathbb{Q}}<q\land q\cdot q<2_{\mathbb{Q}}\}.
   > \]
   > Then
   > \[
   > \sqrt{2}=\sup \iota(S).
   > \]
   > Thus the bounded-above rational set with no rational supremum has a supremum
   > in $\mathbb{R}$.

items.title: Extended Real Addition Is Well Defined
items.statement:
For every pair $(x,y)$ in the domain of extended real addition, there is a
unique element $z\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
\[
z=x+y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every pair $(x,y)$ in the domain of extended real addition, there is a
   > unique element $z\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
   > \[
   > z=x+y.
   > \]

items.title: Extended Addition Extends Real Addition
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
x+_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}y=x+_{\mathbb{R}}y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > x+_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}y=x+_{\mathbb{R}}y.
   > \]

items.title: Addition with Infinities
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
x+(+\infty)=+\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
x+(-\infty)=-\infty.
\]
Moreover,
\[
(+\infty)+(+\infty)=+\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
(-\infty)+(-\infty)=-\infty.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > x+(+\infty)=+\infty
   > \quad\text{and}\quad
   > x+(-\infty)=-\infty.
   > \]
   > Moreover,
   > \[
   > (+\infty)+(+\infty)=+\infty
   > \quad\text{and}\quad
   > (-\infty)+(-\infty)=-\infty.
   > \]

items.title: Extended Real Negation Is Well Defined
items.statement:
For every $x\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$, there is a unique
$y\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
\[
y=-x.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$, there is a unique
   > $y\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
   > \[
   > y=-x.
   > \]

items.title: Extended Real Multiplication Is Well Defined
items.statement:
For every pair $(x,y)$ in the domain of extended real multiplication, there is
a unique element $z\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
\[
z=xy.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every pair $(x,y)$ in the domain of extended real multiplication, there is
   > a unique element $z\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
   > \[
   > z=xy.
   > \]

items.title: Extended Multiplication Extends Real Multiplication
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
x\cdot_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}y=x\cdot_{\mathbb{R}}y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > x\cdot_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}y=x\cdot_{\mathbb{R}}y.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication with Infinities
items.statement:
If $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $x>0$, then
\[
x(+\infty)=+\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
x(-\infty)=-\infty.
\]
If $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $x<0$, then
\[
x(+\infty)=-\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
x(-\infty)=+\infty.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $x>0$, then
   > \[
   > x(+\infty)=+\infty
   > \quad\text{and}\quad
   > x(-\infty)=-\infty.
   > \]
   > If $x\in\mathbb{R}$ and $x<0$, then
   > \[
   > x(+\infty)=-\infty
   > \quad\text{and}\quad
   > x(-\infty)=+\infty.
   > \]

items.title: Indeterminate Extended Real Forms
items.statement:
The expressions
\[
(+\infty)+(-\infty),\qquad
(-\infty)+(+\infty),\qquad
0\cdot(+\infty),\qquad
0\cdot(-\infty)
\]
are not defined in the extended real arithmetic introduced here.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The expressions
   > \[
   > (+\infty)+(-\infty),\qquad
   > (-\infty)+(+\infty),\qquad
   > 0\cdot(+\infty),\qquad
   > 0\cdot(-\infty)
   > \]
   > are not defined in the extended real arithmetic introduced here.

items.title: Real Rays as Extended Intervals
items.statement:
For $a\in\mathbb{R}$, the real rays
\[
(a,+\infty),\qquad [a,+\infty),\qquad
(-\infty,a),\qquad (-\infty,a]
\]
are the finite parts of extended intervals with infinite endpoints.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For $a\in\mathbb{R}$, the real rays
   > \[
   > (a,+\infty),\qquad [a,+\infty),\qquad
   > (-\infty,a),\qquad (-\infty,a]
   > \]
   > are the finite parts of extended intervals with infinite endpoints.

items.title: Extended Closed Rays Contain Infinite Endpoints
items.statement:
For $a\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
+\infty\in [a,+\infty]_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
-\infty\in [-\infty,a]_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For $a\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > +\infty\in [a,+\infty]_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}
   > \quad\text{and}\quad
   > -\infty\in [-\infty,a]_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}.
   > \]

items.title: Comparison with Infinities
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
-\infty<x<+\infty.
\]
Also,
\[
-\infty\le y\le+\infty
\]
for every $y\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > -\infty<x<+\infty.
   > \]
   > Also,
   > \[
   > -\infty\le y\le+\infty
   > \]
   > for every $y\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$.

items.title: The Extended Real Line Is Closed and Bounded
items.statement:
In $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$,
\[
\overline{\mathbb{R}}=[-\infty,+\infty].
\]
Thus the whole extended real line has both a least element and a greatest
element.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > In $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$,
   > \[
   > \overline{\mathbb{R}}=[-\infty,+\infty].
   > \]
   > Thus the whole extended real line has both a least element and a greatest
   > element.

items.title: Extended Interval Order Characterization
items.statement:
A subset $I\subseteq\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ is an extended real interval if and
only if for all $x,z\in I$ with $x\le z$,
\[
[x,z]_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}\subseteq I.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > A subset $I\subseteq\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ is an extended real interval if and
   > only if for all $x,z\in I$ with $x\le z$,
   > \[
   > [x,z]_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}\subseteq I.
   > \]

items.title: Extended Real Order Is Well Defined
items.statement:
The relation $\le_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}$ defines a binary relation on
$\overline{\mathbb{R}}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The relation $\le_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}$ defines a binary relation on
   > $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$.

items.title: Extended Real Order Is Total
items.statement:
The ordered set $(\overline{\mathbb{R}},\le_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}})$ is a
totally ordered set.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The ordered set $(\overline{\mathbb{R}},\le_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}})$ is a
   > totally ordered set.

items.title: Real Order Embeds in the Extended Real Order
items.statement:
For all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
x\le_{\mathbb{R}}y
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\le_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}y.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > x\le_{\mathbb{R}}y
   > \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
   > x\le_{\overline{\mathbb{R}}}y.
   > \]

items.title: Complex Coordinate Equivalence Is Reflexive
items.statement:
For every $(a,b)\in\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{C}$,
\[
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(a,b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $(a,b)\in\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{C}$,
   > \[
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(a,b).
   > \]

items.title: Complex Coordinate Equivalence Is Symmetric
items.statement:
For all prepairs $(a,b),(c,d)$,
\[
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(c,d)
\Longrightarrow
(c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(a,b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all prepairs $(a,b),(c,d)$,
   > \[
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(c,d)
   > \Longrightarrow
   > (c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(a,b).
   > \]

items.title: Complex Coordinate Equivalence Is Transitive
items.statement:
For all prepairs $(a,b),(c,d),(e,f)$,
\[
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(c,d)\land
(c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(e,f)
\Longrightarrow
(a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(e,f).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all prepairs $(a,b),(c,d),(e,f)$,
   > \[
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(c,d)\land
   > (c,d)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(e,f)
   > \Longrightarrow
   > (a,b)\sim_{\mathbb{C}}(e,f).
   > \]

items.title: Complex Coordinate Equivalence Is an Equivalence Relation
items.statement:
The relation $\sim_{\mathbb{C}}$ is an equivalence relation on
\(\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{C}\).
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The relation $\sim_{\mathbb{C}}$ is an equivalence relation on
   > \(\operatorname{Pre}\mathbb{C}\).

items.title: The Real Embedding into $\mathbb{C}$ Is Injective
items.statement: If \(\iota(a)=\iota(b)\), then \(a=b\).
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If \(\iota(a)=\iota(b)\), then \(a=b\).

items.title: The Real Embedding Preserves Addition and Multiplication
items.statement:
For all \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\),
\[
\iota(a+b)=\iota(a)+\iota(b),
\qquad
\iota(ab)=\iota(a)\iota(b).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all \(a,b\in\mathbb{R}\),
   > \[
   > \iota(a+b)=\iota(a)+\iota(b),
   > \qquad
   > \iota(ab)=\iota(a)\iota(b).
   > \]

items.title: The Real Embedding Preserves Zero and One
items.statement:
\[
\iota(0)=0_{\mathbb{C}},
\qquad
\iota(1)=1_{\mathbb{C}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > \[
   > \iota(0)=0_{\mathbb{C}},
   > \qquad
   > \iota(1)=1_{\mathbb{C}}.
   > \]

items.title: Real and Imaginary Parts Are Well-Defined
items.statement:
The functions
\[
\operatorname{Re},\operatorname{Im}:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{R}
\]
are well-defined.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The functions
   > \[
   > \operatorname{Re},\operatorname{Im}:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{R}
   > \]
   > are well-defined.

items.title: Addition Respects Complex Coordinate Equivalence
items.statement:
If $[a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}=[a',b']_{\mathbb{C}}$ and
$[c,d]_{\mathbb{C}}=[c',d']_{\mathbb{C}}$, then
\[
[a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}+[c,d]_{\mathbb{C}}
=
[a',b']_{\mathbb{C}}+[c',d']_{\mathbb{C}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $[a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}=[a',b']_{\mathbb{C}}$ and
   > $[c,d]_{\mathbb{C}}=[c',d']_{\mathbb{C}}$, then
   > \[
   > [a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}+[c,d]_{\mathbb{C}}
   > =
   > [a',b']_{\mathbb{C}}+[c',d']_{\mathbb{C}}.
   > \]

items.title: Addition on $\mathbb{C}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
Addition determines a well-defined binary operation
\[
\mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Addition determines a well-defined binary operation
   > \[
   > \mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}.
   > \]

items.title: Addition on $\mathbb{C}$ Is Associative
items.statement:
For all \(z,w,u\in\mathbb{C}\),
\[
(z+w)+u=z+(w+u).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all \(z,w,u\in\mathbb{C}\),
   > \[
   > (z+w)+u=z+(w+u).
   > \]

items.title: Addition on $\mathbb{C}$ Is Commutative
items.statement:
For all \(z,w\in\mathbb{C}\),
\[
z+w=w+z.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all \(z,w\in\mathbb{C}\),
   > \[
   > z+w=w+z.
   > \]

items.title: Zero Is an Additive Identity on $\mathbb{C}$
items.statement:
For every \(z\in\mathbb{C}\),
\[
0_{\mathbb{C}}+z=z
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
z+0_{\mathbb{C}}=z.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every \(z\in\mathbb{C}\),
   > \[
   > 0_{\mathbb{C}}+z=z
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > z+0_{\mathbb{C}}=z.
   > \]

items.title: Every Complex Number Has an Additive Inverse
items.statement:
For every \(z\in\mathbb{C}\),
\[
z+(-z)=0_{\mathbb{C}}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
(-z)+z=0_{\mathbb{C}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every \(z\in\mathbb{C}\),
   > \[
   > z+(-z)=0_{\mathbb{C}}
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > (-z)+z=0_{\mathbb{C}}.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication Respects Complex Coordinate Equivalence
items.statement:
If $[a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}=[a',b']_{\mathbb{C}}$ and
$[c,d]_{\mathbb{C}}=[c',d']_{\mathbb{C}}$, then
\[
[a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}\cdot[c,d]_{\mathbb{C}}
=
[a',b']_{\mathbb{C}}\cdot[c',d']_{\mathbb{C}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $[a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}=[a',b']_{\mathbb{C}}$ and
   > $[c,d]_{\mathbb{C}}=[c',d']_{\mathbb{C}}$, then
   > \[
   > [a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}\cdot[c,d]_{\mathbb{C}}
   > =
   > [a',b']_{\mathbb{C}}\cdot[c',d']_{\mathbb{C}}.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication on $\mathbb{C}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
Multiplication determines a well-defined binary operation
\[
\mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Multiplication determines a well-defined binary operation
   > \[
   > \mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication on $\mathbb{C}$ Is Associative
items.statement:
For all \(z,w,u\in\mathbb{C}\),
\[
(zw)u=z(wu).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all \(z,w,u\in\mathbb{C}\),
   > \[
   > (zw)u=z(wu).
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication on $\mathbb{C}$ Is Commutative
items.statement:
For all \(z,w\in\mathbb{C}\),
\[
zw=wz.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all \(z,w\in\mathbb{C}\),
   > \[
   > zw=wz.
   > \]

items.title: One Is a Multiplicative Identity on $\mathbb{C}$
items.statement:
For every \(z\in\mathbb{C}\),
\[
1_{\mathbb{C}}z=z
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
z1_{\mathbb{C}}=z.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every \(z\in\mathbb{C}\),
   > \[
   > 1_{\mathbb{C}}z=z
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > z1_{\mathbb{C}}=z.
   > \]

items.title:
Product with the Con
jugate Is Real and Nonnegative
items.statement:
For \(z=[a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}\),
\[
z\overline{z}=[a^2+b^2,0]_{\mathbb{C}}.
\]
Moreover, if \(z\ne 0_{\mathbb{C}}\), then \(a^2+b^2\ne 0\).
items.markdown:
jugate Is Real and Nonnegative**
   > **Statement.**
   > For \(z=[a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}\),
   > \[
   > z\overline{z}=[a^2+b^2,0]_{\mathbb{C}}.
   > \]
   > Moreover, if \(z\ne 0_{\mathbb{C}}\), then \(a^2+b^2\ne 0\).

items.title: Inversion on $\mathbb{C}^{\times}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement: Inversion determines a well-defined operation on the nonzero complex numbers.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Inversion determines a well-defined operation on the nonzero complex numbers.

items.title: Every Nonzero Complex Number Has a Multiplicative Inverse
items.statement:
For every \(z\in\mathbb{C}\) with \(z\ne 0_{\mathbb{C}}\),
\[
zz^{-1}=1_{\mathbb{C}}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
z^{-1}z=1_{\mathbb{C}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every \(z\in\mathbb{C}\) with \(z\ne 0_{\mathbb{C}}\),
   > \[
   > zz^{-1}=1_{\mathbb{C}}
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > z^{-1}z=1_{\mathbb{C}}.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication Distributes over Addition on $\mathbb{C}$
items.statement:
For all \(z,w,u\in\mathbb{C}\),
\[
z(w+u)=zw+zu
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
(w+u)z=wz+uz.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all \(z,w,u\in\mathbb{C}\),
   > \[
   > z(w+u)=zw+zu
   > \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   > (w+u)z=wz+uz.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{C}$ Is a Field
items.statement:
With the operations defined above,
\[
(\mathbb{C},+,\,\cdot,\,0_{\mathbb{C}},\,1_{\mathbb{C}})
\]
is a field.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > With the operations defined above,
   > \[
   > (\mathbb{C},+,\,\cdot,\,0_{\mathbb{C}},\,1_{\mathbb{C}})
   > \]
   > is a field.

items.title: The Imaginary Unit Squares to Negative One
items.statement:
In \(\mathbb{C}\),
\[
i^2=-1_{\mathbb{C}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > In \(\mathbb{C}\),
   > \[
   > i^2=-1_{\mathbb{C}}.
   > \]

items.title: $\mathbb{C}$ Is Not an Ordered Field
items.statement:
There is no order relation on \(\mathbb{C}\) making \(\mathbb{C}\) an ordered
field and extending the usual order on \(\mathbb{R}\).
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > There is no order relation on \(\mathbb{C}\) making \(\mathbb{C}\) an ordered
   > field and extending the usual order on \(\mathbb{R}\).

items.title: Negation Respects Complex Coordinate Equivalence
items.statement:
If $[a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}=[a',b']_{\mathbb{C}}$, then
\[
-[a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}=-[a',b']_{\mathbb{C}}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $[a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}=[a',b']_{\mathbb{C}}$, then
   > \[
   > -[a,b]_{\mathbb{C}}=-[a',b']_{\mathbb{C}}.
   > \]

items.title: Negation on $\mathbb{C}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement: Negation determines a well-defined unary operation $\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Negation determines a well-defined unary operation $\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$.

items.title: Subtraction on $\mathbb{C}$ Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
Subtraction determines a well-defined binary operation
\(\mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}\).
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Subtraction determines a well-defined binary operation
   > \(\mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}\).

items.title: Complex Conjugation Is Well-Defined
items.statement:
Complex conjugation determines a well-defined unary operation
\(\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}\).
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Complex conjugation determines a well-defined unary operation
   > \(\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}\).

items.title: Embeddings Identify a System with Its Image
items.statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be an embedding of ordered arithmetic systems relative to
a selected source structure. Then the corestriction $\varphi:A\to\varphi(A)$
is an isomorphism onto its image: it is a bijection that preserves and reflects
the selected constants, operations, and order. Consequently $A$ may be
identified with the corresponding substructure $\varphi(A)\subseteq B$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be an embedding of ordered arithmetic systems relative to
   > a selected source structure. Then the corestriction $\varphi:A\to\varphi(A)$
   > is an isomorphism onto its image: it is a bijection that preserves and reflects
   > the selected constants, operations, and order. Consequently $A$ may be
   > identified with the corresponding substructure $\varphi(A)\subseteq B$.

items.title: $\mathbb{Q}$ Embeds in $\mathbb{R}$
items.statement: The canonical map $\iota:\mathbb{Q}\to \mathbb{R}$ is an embedding of ordered arithmetic systems: it is injective, preserves $0$, $1$, addition, and multiplication, and reflects the order.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The canonical map $\iota:\mathbb{Q}\to \mathbb{R}$ is an embedding of ordered arithmetic systems: it is injective, preserves $0$, $1$, addition, and multiplication, and reflects the order.

items.title: $\mathbb{W}$ Embeds in $\mathbb{Z}$
items.statement: The canonical map $\iota:\mathbb{W}\to \mathbb{Z}$ is an embedding of ordered arithmetic systems: it is injective, preserves $0$, $1$, addition, and multiplication, and reflects the order.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The canonical map $\iota:\mathbb{W}\to \mathbb{Z}$ is an embedding of ordered arithmetic systems: it is injective, preserves $0$, $1$, addition, and multiplication, and reflects the order.

items.title: $\mathbb{Z}$ Embeds in $\mathbb{Q}$
items.statement: The canonical map $\iota:\mathbb{Z}\to \mathbb{Q}$ is an embedding of ordered arithmetic systems: it is injective, preserves $0$, $1$, addition, and multiplication, and reflects the order.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The canonical map $\iota:\mathbb{Z}\to \mathbb{Q}$ is an embedding of ordered arithmetic systems: it is injective, preserves $0$, $1$, addition, and multiplication, and reflects the order.

items.title: Compatibility of the Embedding Chain
items.statement: Let $\iota_{1}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{W}$, $\iota_{2}:\mathbb{W}\to\mathbb{Z}$, $\iota_{3}:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Q}$, and $\iota_{4}:\mathbb{Q}\to\mathbb{R}$ be the canonical embeddings. For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ the composite $(\iota_{4}\circ\iota_{3}\circ\iota_{2}\circ\iota_{1})(n)$ is the real number identified with $n$, and the composite preserves the arithmetic and order carried by the source system. Hence arithmetic computed in any system agrees with arithmetic on its image in $\mathbb{R}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $\iota_{1}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{W}$, $\iota_{2}:\mathbb{W}\to\mathbb{Z}$, $\iota_{3}:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Q}$, and $\iota_{4}:\mathbb{Q}\to\mathbb{R}$ be the canonical embeddings. For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ the composite $(\iota_{4}\circ\iota_{3}\circ\iota_{2}\circ\iota_{1})(n)$ is the real number identified with $n$, and the composite preserves the arithmetic and order carried by the source system. Hence arithmetic computed in any system agrees with arithmetic on its image in $\mathbb{R}$.

items.title: $\mathbb{N}$ Embeds in $\mathbb{W}$
items.statement:
The canonical map $\iota:\mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{W}$ identifies $\mathbb{N}$ with
the positive part $\mathbb{W}\setminus\{0\}$ and preserves successor, $1$,
addition, multiplication, and order.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > The canonical map $\iota:\mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{W}$ identifies $\mathbb{N}$ with
   > the positive part $\mathbb{W}\setminus\{0\}$ and preserves successor, $1$,
   > addition, multiplication, and order.

items.title: Little-o Quotient Characterisation
items.statement:
Let $a\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $f$ and $g$ be real-valued functions defined on a
punctured neighbourhood of $a$, with $g(x)\neq 0$ for $x$ sufficiently close to
$a$ and $x\neq a$. Then
\[
 f(x)=o(g(x))\ (x\to a)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\to 0\ (x\to a).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $a\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $f$ and $g$ be real-valued functions defined on a
   > punctured neighbourhood of $a$, with $g(x)\neq 0$ for $x$ sufficiently close to
   > $a$ and $x\neq a$. Then
   > \[
   >  f(x)=o(g(x))\ (x\to a)
   >  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
   >  \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\to 0\ (x\to a).
   > \]

items.title: Sum Rule for Little-o
items.statement:
If $f_1(x)=o(g(x))$ and $f_2(x)=o(g(x))$ as $x\to a$, then
\[
 f_1(x)+f_2(x)=o(g(x))\qquad (x\to a).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $f_1(x)=o(g(x))$ and $f_2(x)=o(g(x))$ as $x\to a$, then
   > \[
   >  f_1(x)+f_2(x)=o(g(x))\qquad (x\to a).
   > \]

items.title: Bounded Factor Rule for Little-o
items.statement:
If $f(x)=o(g(x))$ as $x\to a$ and $m$ is bounded near $a$, then
\[
 m(x)f(x)=o(g(x))\qquad (x\to a).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $f(x)=o(g(x))$ as $x\to a$ and $m$ is bounded near $a$, then
   > \[
   >  m(x)f(x)=o(g(x))\qquad (x\to a).
   > \]

items.title: Addition Preserves Strict Inequality
items.statement:
For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 a < b \;\Rightarrow\; a + c < b + c.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  a < b \;\Rightarrow\; a + c < b + c.
   > \]

items.title: Addition Preserves Nonstrict Inequality
items.statement:
For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 a \le b \;\Rightarrow\; a + c \le b + c.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  a \le b \;\Rightarrow\; a + c \le b + c.
   > \]

items.title: Transitivity of Strict Inequality
items.statement:
For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 a < b \;\land\; b < c \;\Rightarrow\; a < c.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  a < b \;\land\; b < c \;\Rightarrow\; a < c.
   > \]

items.title: Addition of Strict Inequalities
items.statement:
For all $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 a < b \;\land\; c < d \;\Rightarrow\; a + c < b + d.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  a < b \;\land\; c < d \;\Rightarrow\; a + c < b + d.
   > \]

items.title: Addition of Nonstrict Inequalities
items.statement:
For all $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 a \le b \;\land\; c \le d \;\Rightarrow\; a + c \le b + d.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  a \le b \;\land\; c \le d \;\Rightarrow\; a + c \le b + d.
   > \]

items.title: Mixed Transitivity
items.statement:
For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 a \le b \;\land\; b < c \;\Rightarrow\; a < c.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  a \le b \;\land\; b < c \;\Rightarrow\; a < c.
   > \]

items.title: Mixed Addition of Inequalities
items.statement:
For all $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 a \le b \;\land\; c < d \;\Rightarrow\; a + c < b + d.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  a \le b \;\land\; c < d \;\Rightarrow\; a + c < b + d.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication by a Positive Scalar Preserves Strict Inequality
items.statement:
For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 a < b \;\land\; 0 < c \;\Rightarrow\; ac < bc.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  a < b \;\land\; 0 < c \;\Rightarrow\; ac < bc.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication by a Negative Scalar Reverses Strict Inequality
items.statement:
For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 a < b \;\land\; c < 0 \;\Rightarrow\; ac > bc.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  a < b \;\land\; c < 0 \;\Rightarrow\; ac > bc.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication by a Positive Scalar Preserves Nonstrict Inequality
items.statement:
For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 a \le b \;\land\; 0 < c \;\Rightarrow\; ac \le bc.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  a \le b \;\land\; 0 < c \;\Rightarrow\; ac \le bc.
   > \]

items.title: Multiplication by a Nonneg Scalar Preserves Nonstrict Inequality
items.statement:
For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 a \le b \;\land\; 0 \le c \;\Rightarrow\; ac \le bc.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  a \le b \;\land\; 0 \le c \;\Rightarrow\; ac \le bc.
   > \]

items.title: Positive Product
items.statement:
If $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, $a>0$, and $b>0$, then
\[
ab>0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, $a>0$, and $b>0$, then
   > \[
   > ab>0.
   > \]

items.title: Negative Times Negative Is Positive
items.statement:
If $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, $a<0$, and $b<0$, then
\[
ab>0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, $a<0$, and $b<0$, then
   > \[
   > ab>0.
   > \]

items.title: Positive Times Negative Is Negative
items.statement:
If $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, $a>0$, and $b<0$, then
\[
ab<0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, $a>0$, and $b<0$, then
   > \[
   > ab<0.
   > \]

items.title: Negative Times Positive Is Negative
items.statement:
If $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, $a<0$, and $b>0$, then
\[
ab<0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$, $a<0$, and $b>0$, then
   > \[
   > ab<0.
   > \]

items.title: Order and Subtraction
items.statement:
For $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
a<b \;\Longleftrightarrow\; b-a>0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > a<b \;\Longleftrightarrow\; b-a>0.
   > \]

items.title: Non-Strict Order and Subtraction
items.statement:
For $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$,
\[
a\le b \;\Longleftrightarrow\; b-a\ge 0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   > a\le b \;\Longleftrightarrow\; b-a\ge 0.
   > \]

items.title: Division by Positive Preserves Order
items.statement:
If $a,b,c\in\mathbb{R}$, $a<b$, and $c>0$, then
\[
\frac ac<\frac bc.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $a,b,c\in\mathbb{R}$, $a<b$, and $c>0$, then
   > \[
   > \frac ac<\frac bc.
   > \]

items.title: Division by Negative Reverses Order
items.statement:
If $a,b,c\in\mathbb{R}$, $a<b$, and $c<0$, then
\[
\frac bc<\frac ac.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $a,b,c\in\mathbb{R}$, $a<b$, and $c<0$, then
   > \[
   > \frac bc<\frac ac.
   > \]

items.title: Squeeze
items.statement:
For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 a \le b \le c \;\land\; a = c \;\Rightarrow\; b = a.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  a \le b \le c \;\land\; a = c \;\Rightarrow\; b = a.
   > \]

items.title: Reciprocal Reverses Strict Inequality for Positives
items.statement:
For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 0 < a < b \;\Rightarrow\; 0 < \frac{1}{b} < \frac{1}{a}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  0 < a < b \;\Rightarrow\; 0 < \frac{1}{b} < \frac{1}{a}.
   > \]

items.title: Reciprocal Equivalence for Positives
items.statement:
For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a > 0$ and $b > 0$,
\[
 a < b \iff \frac{1}{b} < \frac{1}{a}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a > 0$ and $b > 0$,
   > \[
   >  a < b \iff \frac{1}{b} < \frac{1}{a}.
   > \]

items.title: Positive Powers Are Positive
items.statement:
If $x>0$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, then
\[
x^n>0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $x>0$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, then
   > \[
   > x^n>0.
   > \]

items.title: Powers Preserve Order for Positive Numbers
items.statement:
If $0<x<y$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, then
\[
x^n<y^n.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $0<x<y$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, then
   > \[
   > x^n<y^n.
   > \]

items.title: Square Is Strictly Monotone on Nonneg Reals
items.statement:
For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 0 \le a < b \;\Rightarrow\; a^2 < b^2.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  0 \le a < b \;\Rightarrow\; a^2 < b^2.
   > \]

items.title: Square Root Is Monotone on Nonneg Reals
items.statement:
For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 0 \le a \le b \;\Rightarrow\; \sqrt{a} \le \sqrt{b}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  0 \le a \le b \;\Rightarrow\; \sqrt{a} \le \sqrt{b}.
   > \]

items.title: AM-GM Inequality for Two Terms
items.statement:
For all $a, b \ge 0$,
\[
 \sqrt{ab} \le \frac{a + b}{2}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b \ge 0$,
   > \[
   >  \sqrt{ab} \le \frac{a + b}{2}.
   > \]

items.title: Bernoulli's Inequality
items.statement:
For all $x \in \mathbb{R}$ with $x \ge -1$ and all $n \in \mathbb{N}$,
\[
 (1 + x)^n \ge 1 + nx.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $x \in \mathbb{R}$ with $x \ge -1$ and all $n \in \mathbb{N}$,
   > \[
   >  (1 + x)^n \ge 1 + nx.
   > \]

items.title: Absolute Value Is Nonnegative
items.statement:
For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 \lvert a \rvert \ge 0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  \lvert a \rvert \ge 0.
   > \]

items.title: Absolute Value Zero Iff Zero
items.statement:
For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 \lvert a \rvert = 0 \iff a = 0.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  \lvert a \rvert = 0 \iff a = 0.
   > \]

items.title: Absolute Value Equals Self or Negation
items.statement:
For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$, either $\lvert a \rvert = a$ or
$\lvert a \rvert = -a$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$, either $\lvert a \rvert = a$ or
   > $\lvert a \rvert = -a$.

items.title: Absolute Value Is Symmetric
items.statement:
For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 \lvert -a \rvert = \lvert a \rvert.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  \lvert -a \rvert = \lvert a \rvert.
   > \]

items.title: Absolute Value of a Product
items.statement:
For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 \lvert ab \rvert = \lvert a \rvert\,\lvert b \rvert.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  \lvert ab \rvert = \lvert a \rvert\,\lvert b \rvert.
   > \]

items.title: Absolute Value of a Quotient
items.statement:
For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and $b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $b \ne 0$,
\[
 \left\lvert \frac{a}{b} \right\rvert
 = \frac{\lvert a \rvert}{\lvert b \rvert}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and $b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $b \ne 0$,
   > \[
   >  \left\lvert \frac{a}{b} \right\rvert
   >  = \frac{\lvert a \rvert}{\lvert b \rvert}.
   > \]

items.title: Bound by Modulus
items.statement:
For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 -\lvert a \rvert \le a \le \lvert a \rvert.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  -\lvert a \rvert \le a \le \lvert a \rvert.
   > \]

items.title: Nonstrict Modulus Inequality
items.statement:
For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and $r \ge 0$,
\[
 \lvert a \rvert \le r \iff -r \le a \le r.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and $r \ge 0$,
   > \[
   >  \lvert a \rvert \le r \iff -r \le a \le r.
   > \]

items.title: Strict Modulus Inequality
items.statement:
For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and $r > 0$,
\[
 \lvert a \rvert < r \iff -r < a < r.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and $r > 0$,
   > \[
   >  \lvert a \rvert < r \iff -r < a < r.
   > \]

items.title: Reverse Triangle Inequality
items.statement:
For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 \lvert\, \lvert a \rvert - \lvert b \rvert \,\rvert
 \le \lvert a - b \rvert.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  \lvert\, \lvert a \rvert - \lvert b \rvert \,\rvert
   >  \le \lvert a - b \rvert.
   > \]

items.title: Generalised Triangle Inequality
items.statement:
For all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $a_1, \ldots, a_n \in \mathbb{R}$,
\[
 \left\lvert \sum_{k=1}^{n} a_k \right\rvert
 \le \sum_{k=1}^{n} \lvert a_k \rvert.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $a_1, \ldots, a_n \in \mathbb{R}$,
   > \[
   >  \left\lvert \sum_{k=1}^{n} a_k \right\rvert
   >  \le \sum_{k=1}^{n} \lvert a_k \rvert.
   > \]

items.title: Order arithmetic
items.statement:
Let $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{R}$.
- [label=(\roman*)]
- If $a\leq b$ and $c\leq d$, then $a+c\leq b+d$.
- If $a\leq b$ and $c>0$, then $ac\leq bc$.
- If $a\leq b$ and $c<0$, then $ac\geq bc$.
- $|x|\leq y$ (with $y\geq 0$) if and only if $-y\leq x\leq y$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{R}$.
   > - [label=(\roman*)]
   > - If $a\leq b$ and $c\leq d$, then $a+c\leq b+d$.
   > - If $a\leq b$ and $c>0$, then $ac\leq bc$.
   > - If $a\leq b$ and $c<0$, then $ac\geq bc$.
   > - $|x|\leq y$ (with $y\geq 0$) if and only if $-y\leq x\leq y$.

items.title: Convergent sequences are bounded
items.statement:
If $(b_n)\to b$, then there exists $M>0$ such that $|b_n|\leq M$ for all
$n\in\mathbb{N}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $(b_n)\to b$, then there exists $M>0$ such that $|b_n|\leq M$ for all
   > $n\in\mathbb{N}$.

items.title: $\varepsilon$-characterisation of $\sup$
items.statement:
Let $S\subset\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above, and let
$s=\sup S$. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $x\in S$ with
$x>s-\varepsilon$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $S\subset\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above, and let
   > $s=\sup S$. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $x\in S$ with
   > $x>s-\varepsilon$.

items.title: Monotone Approximation of Bounds
items.statement:
Let $S\subset\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded. Then there exist
monotone sequences $(x_n),(y_n)\subset S$ with
$x_n\to\sup S$ and $y_n\to\inf S$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $S\subset\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded. Then there exist
   > monotone sequences $(x_n),(y_n)\subset S$ with
   > $x_n\to\sup S$ and $y_n\to\inf S$.

items.title: The dichotomy
items.statement:
For any predicate $P$ on $\mathbb{N}$, exactly one of the following holds:
- [label=(\roman*)]
- $P$ holds infinitely often.
- $\neg P$ holds eventually.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For any predicate $P$ on $\mathbb{N}$, exactly one of the following holds:
   > - [label=(\roman*)]
   > - $P$ holds infinitely often.
   > - $\neg P$ holds eventually.

items.title: Bolzano--Weierstrass via bisection
items.statement: Every bounded sequence in $\mathbb{R}$ has a convergent subsequence.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Every bounded sequence in $\mathbb{R}$ has a convergent subsequence.

items.title: Intermediate Value Theorem
items.statement:
Let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous. If $L\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfies
$f(a)<L<f(b)$ or $f(a)>L>f(b)$, then there exists $c\in(a,b)$ with
$f(c)=L$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous. If $L\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfies
   > $f(a)<L<f(b)$ or $f(a)>L>f(b)$, then there exists $c\in(a,b)$ with
   > $f(c)=L$.

items.title: R Uncountable
items.statement: $\mathbb{R}$ is uncountable.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > $\mathbb{R}$ is uncountable.

items.title: Residue divergence criterion
items.statement:
If there exist residues $r, s \in \{0,\ldots,k-1\}$ such that
$(a_{kn+r}) \to L$ and $(a_{kn+s}) \to M$ with $L \neq M$, then
$(a_n)$ diverges.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If there exist residues $r, s \in \{0,\ldots,k-1\}$ such that
   > $(a_{kn+r}) \to L$ and $(a_{kn+s}) \to M$ with $L \neq M$, then
   > $(a_n)$ diverges.

items.title: Supremum of a Reciprocal Set
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded, and suppose that
$0<\inf A$ or $\sup A<0$. Define
\[
 A^{-1}:=\{1/a:a\in A\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \sup(A^{-1})=\frac{1}{\inf A}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded, and suppose that
   > $0<\inf A$ or $\sup A<0$. Define
   > \[
   >  A^{-1}:=\{1/a:a\in A\}.
   > \]
   > Then
   > \[
   >  \sup(A^{-1})=\frac{1}{\inf A}.
   > \]

items.title: Infimum of a Reciprocal Set
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded, and suppose that
$0<\inf A$ or $\sup A<0$. Define
\[
 A^{-1}:=\{1/a:a\in A\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \inf(A^{-1})=\frac{1}{\sup A}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded, and suppose that
   > $0<\inf A$ or $\sup A<0$. Define
   > \[
   >  A^{-1}:=\{1/a:a\in A\}.
   > \]
   > Then
   > \[
   >  \inf(A^{-1})=\frac{1}{\sup A}.
   > \]

items.title: Supremum of a Product Set
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded. Then
\[
 \sup(AB)=
 \max\{(\inf A)(\inf B),(\inf A)(\sup B),(\sup A)(\inf B),(\sup A)(\sup B)\}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded. Then
   > \[
   >  \sup(AB)=
   >  \max\{(\inf A)(\inf B),(\inf A)(\sup B),(\sup A)(\inf B),(\sup A)(\sup B)\}.
   > \]

items.title: Infimum of a Product Set
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded. Then
\[
 \inf(AB)=
 \min\{(\inf A)(\inf B),(\inf A)(\sup B),(\sup A)(\inf B),(\sup A)(\sup B)\}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded. Then
   > \[
   >  \inf(AB)=
   >  \min\{(\inf A)(\inf B),(\inf A)(\sup B),(\sup A)(\inf B),(\sup A)(\sup B)\}.
   > \]

items.title: Supremum of a Quotient Set
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded, and suppose
$0<\inf B$ or $\sup B<0$. Then
\[
 \sup(A/B)=
 \max\left\{\frac{\inf A}{\inf B},\frac{\inf A}{\sup B},
 \frac{\sup A}{\inf B},\frac{\sup A}{\sup B}\right\}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded, and suppose
   > $0<\inf B$ or $\sup B<0$. Then
   > \[
   >  \sup(A/B)=
   >  \max\left\{\frac{\inf A}{\inf B},\frac{\inf A}{\sup B},
   >  \frac{\sup A}{\inf B},\frac{\sup A}{\sup B}\right\}.
   > \]

items.title: Infimum of a Quotient Set
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded, and suppose
$0<\inf B$ or $\sup B<0$. Then
\[
 \inf(A/B)=
 \min\left\{\frac{\inf A}{\inf B},\frac{\inf A}{\sup B},
 \frac{\sup A}{\inf B},\frac{\sup A}{\sup B}\right\}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded, and suppose
   > $0<\inf B$ or $\sup B<0$. Then
   > \[
   >  \inf(A/B)=
   >  \min\left\{\frac{\inf A}{\inf B},\frac{\inf A}{\sup B},
   >  \frac{\sup A}{\inf B},\frac{\sup A}{\sup B}\right\}.
   > \]

items.title: Bounds for Suprema and Infima Under Set Addition
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded. Then
\[
 \inf A+\inf B\le \inf(A+B)
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \sup(A+B)\le \sup A+\sup B.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded. Then
   > \[
   >  \inf A+\inf B\le \inf(A+B)
   >  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
   >  \sup(A+B)\le \sup A+\sup B.
   > \]

items.title: Upper Bounds Depend on the Ambient Order
items.statement: Let $(S,\le_S)$ and $(T,\le_T)$ be ordered sets, and let $A\subseteq S\cap T$. Whether $u$ is an upper bound of $A$ must be interpreted relative to the chosen ambient order.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(S,\le_S)$ and $(T,\le_T)$ be ordered sets, and let $A\subseteq S\cap T$. Whether $u$ is an upper bound of $A$ must be interpreted relative to the chosen ambient order.

items.title: Suprema Depend on the Ambient Set
items.statement: Let $A\subseteq S\subseteq S'$ be subsets of an ordered set. The supremum of $A$ relative to $S$, if it exists, need not agree with the supremum of $A$ relative to $S'$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq S\subseteq S'$ be subsets of an ordered set. The supremum of $A$ relative to $S$, if it exists, need not agree with the supremum of $A$ relative to $S'$.

items.title: Ambient Existence of Supremum
items.statement: There are ordered sets $S\subseteq S'$ and a subset $A\subseteq S$ such that $A$ has a supremum relative to $S'$ but has no supremum relative to $S$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > There are ordered sets $S\subseteq S'$ and a subset $A\subseteq S$ such that $A$ has a supremum relative to $S'$ but has no supremum relative to $S$.

items.title: Rational Gap Example for Suprema
items.statement:
Let
\[
 A=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:q^2<2\}.
\]
Then $A$ is nonempty and bounded above in $\mathbb{Q}$, but $A$ has no supremum relative to $\mathbb{Q}$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let
   > \[
   >  A=\{q\in\mathbb{Q}:q^2<2\}.
   > \]
   > Then $A$ is nonempty and bounded above in $\mathbb{Q}$, but $A$ has no supremum relative to $\mathbb{Q}$.

items.title: Translation Preserves Upper Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty. If $u$ is an upper bound of $A$,
then $u+c$ is an upper bound of $A+c$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty. If $u$ is an upper bound of $A$,
   > then $u+c$ is an upper bound of $A+c$.

items.title: Translation Preserves Lower Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty. If $\ell$ is a lower bound of $A$,
then $\ell+c$ is a lower bound of $A+c$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty. If $\ell$ is a lower bound of $A$,
   > then $\ell+c$ is a lower bound of $A+c$.

items.title: Positive Dilation Preserves Upper Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and let $\lambda>0$. If $u$ is an
upper bound of $A$, then $\lambda u$ is an upper bound of $\lambda A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and let $\lambda>0$. If $u$ is an
   > upper bound of $A$, then $\lambda u$ is an upper bound of $\lambda A$.

items.title: Positive Dilation Preserves Lower Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and let $\lambda>0$. If $\ell$ is a
lower bound of $A$, then $\lambda\ell$ is a lower bound of $\lambda A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and let $\lambda>0$. If $\ell$ is a
   > lower bound of $A$, then $\lambda\ell$ is a lower bound of $\lambda A$.

items.title: Negative Dilation Sends Lower Bounds to Upper Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and let $\lambda<0$. If $\ell$ is a
lower bound of $A$, then $\lambda\ell$ is an upper bound of $\lambda A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and let $\lambda<0$. If $\ell$ is a
   > lower bound of $A$, then $\lambda\ell$ is an upper bound of $\lambda A$.

items.title: Negative Dilation Sends Upper Bounds to Lower Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and let $\lambda<0$. If $u$ is an
upper bound of $A$, then $\lambda u$ is a lower bound of $\lambda A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and let $\lambda<0$. If $u$ is an
   > upper bound of $A$, then $\lambda u$ is a lower bound of $\lambda A$.

items.title: Reflection Swaps Upper and Lower Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty. If $\ell$ is a lower bound of $A$,
then $-\ell$ is an upper bound of $-A$. If $u$ is an upper bound of $A$,
then $-u$ is a lower bound of $-A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty. If $\ell$ is a lower bound of $A$,
   > then $-\ell$ is an upper bound of $-A$. If $u$ is an upper bound of $A$,
   > then $-u$ is a lower bound of $-A$.

items.title: Increasing Image Preserves Suprema
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, let $A\subseteq I$ be nonempty and bounded above,
and let $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ be increasing. Suppose $s=\sup A$ belongs to $I$
and $f$ is continuous at $s$. Then
\[
 \sup f(A)=f(\sup A),
 \qquad
 f(A)=\{f(a):a\in A\}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, let $A\subseteq I$ be nonempty and bounded above,
   > and let $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ be increasing. Suppose $s=\sup A$ belongs to $I$
   > and $f$ is continuous at $s$. Then
   > \[
   >  \sup f(A)=f(\sup A),
   >  \qquad
   >  f(A)=\{f(a):a\in A\}.
   > \]

items.title: Increasing Image Preserves Infima
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, let $A\subseteq I$ be nonempty and bounded below,
and let $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ be increasing. Suppose $t=\inf A$ belongs to $I$
and $f$ is continuous at $t$. Then
\[
 \inf f(A)=f(\inf A).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, let $A\subseteq I$ be nonempty and bounded below,
   > and let $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ be increasing. Suppose $t=\inf A$ belongs to $I$
   > and $f$ is continuous at $t$. Then
   > \[
   >  \inf f(A)=f(\inf A).
   > \]

items.title: Decreasing Image Sends Infimum to Supremum
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, let $A\subseteq I$ be nonempty and bounded below,
and let $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ be decreasing. Suppose $t=\inf A$ belongs to $I$
and $f$ is continuous at $t$. Then
\[
 \sup f(A)=f(\inf A).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, let $A\subseteq I$ be nonempty and bounded below,
   > and let $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ be decreasing. Suppose $t=\inf A$ belongs to $I$
   > and $f$ is continuous at $t$. Then
   > \[
   >  \sup f(A)=f(\inf A).
   > \]

items.title: Decreasing Image Sends Supremum to Infimum
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, let $A\subseteq I$ be nonempty and bounded above,
and let $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ be decreasing. Suppose $s=\sup A$ belongs to $I$
and $f$ is continuous at $s$. Then
\[
 \inf f(A)=f(\sup A).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, let $A\subseteq I$ be nonempty and bounded above,
   > and let $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ be decreasing. Suppose $s=\sup A$ belongs to $I$
   > and $f$ is continuous at $s$. Then
   > \[
   >  \inf f(A)=f(\sup A).
   > \]

items.title: Increasing Inverse Preserves Suprema
items.statement:
Let $I,J\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, and let $f:I\to J$ be bijective. Suppose
$f^{-1}:J\to I$ is increasing and continuous. If $B\subseteq J$ is nonempty
and bounded above, and if $\sup B\in J$, then
\[
 \sup f^{-1}(B)=f^{-1}(\sup B).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $I,J\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, and let $f:I\to J$ be bijective. Suppose
   > $f^{-1}:J\to I$ is increasing and continuous. If $B\subseteq J$ is nonempty
   > and bounded above, and if $\sup B\in J$, then
   > \[
   >  \sup f^{-1}(B)=f^{-1}(\sup B).
   > \]

items.title: Increasing Inverse Preserves Infima
items.statement:
Let $I,J\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, and let $f:I\to J$ be bijective. Suppose
$f^{-1}:J\to I$ is increasing and continuous. If $B\subseteq J$ is nonempty
and bounded below, and if $\inf B\in J$, then
\[
 \inf f^{-1}(B)=f^{-1}(\inf B).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $I,J\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, and let $f:I\to J$ be bijective. Suppose
   > $f^{-1}:J\to I$ is increasing and continuous. If $B\subseteq J$ is nonempty
   > and bounded below, and if $\inf B\in J$, then
   > \[
   >  \inf f^{-1}(B)=f^{-1}(\inf B).
   > \]

items.title: Decreasing Inverse Sends Infimum to Supremum
items.statement:
Let $I,J\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, and let $f:I\to J$ be bijective. Suppose
$f^{-1}:J\to I$ is decreasing and continuous. If $B\subseteq J$ is nonempty
and bounded below, and if $\inf B\in J$, then
\[
 \sup f^{-1}(B)=f^{-1}(\inf B).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $I,J\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, and let $f:I\to J$ be bijective. Suppose
   > $f^{-1}:J\to I$ is decreasing and continuous. If $B\subseteq J$ is nonempty
   > and bounded below, and if $\inf B\in J$, then
   > \[
   >  \sup f^{-1}(B)=f^{-1}(\inf B).
   > \]

items.title: Decreasing Inverse Sends Supremum to Infimum
items.statement:
Let $I,J\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, and let $f:I\to J$ be bijective. Suppose
$f^{-1}:J\to I$ is decreasing and continuous. If $B\subseteq J$ is nonempty
and bounded above, and if $\sup B\in J$, then
\[
 \inf f^{-1}(B)=f^{-1}(\sup B).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $I,J\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, and let $f:I\to J$ be bijective. Suppose
   > $f^{-1}:J\to I$ is decreasing and continuous. If $B\subseteq J$ is nonempty
   > and bounded above, and if $\sup B\in J$, then
   > \[
   >  \inf f^{-1}(B)=f^{-1}(\sup B).
   > \]

items.title: Supremum of the Pointwise Maximum Set
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above. Then
\[
 \sup\max(A,B)=\max\{\sup A,\sup B\}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above. Then
   > \[
   >  \sup\max(A,B)=\max\{\sup A,\sup B\}.
   > \]

items.title: Infimum of the Pointwise Maximum Set
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below. Then
\[
 \inf\max(A,B)=\max\{\inf A,\inf B\}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below. Then
   > \[
   >  \inf\max(A,B)=\max\{\inf A,\inf B\}.
   > \]

items.title: Supremum of the Pointwise Minimum Set
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above. Then
\[
 \sup\min(A,B)=\min\{\sup A,\sup B\}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above. Then
   > \[
   >  \sup\min(A,B)=\min\{\sup A,\sup B\}.
   > \]

items.title: Infimum of the Pointwise Minimum Set
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below. Then
\[
 \inf\min(A,B)=\min\{\inf A,\inf B\}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below. Then
   > \[
   >  \inf\min(A,B)=\min\{\inf A,\inf B\}.
   > \]

items.title: Union Preserves Upper Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. If $u_A$ is an upper bound of $A$ and
$u_B$ is an upper bound of $B$, then $\max\{u_A,u_B\}$ is an upper bound
of $A\cup B$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. If $u_A$ is an upper bound of $A$ and
   > $u_B$ is an upper bound of $B$, then $\max\{u_A,u_B\}$ is an upper bound
   > of $A\cup B$.

items.title: Union Preserves Lower Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. If $\ell_A$ is a lower bound of $A$ and
$\ell_B$ is a lower bound of $B$, then $\min\{\ell_A,\ell_B\}$ is a lower
bound of $A\cup B$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. If $\ell_A$ is a lower bound of $A$ and
   > $\ell_B$ is a lower bound of $B$, then $\min\{\ell_A,\ell_B\}$ is a lower
   > bound of $A\cup B$.

items.title: Subsets Preserve Upper Bounds
items.statement:
Let $C\subseteq A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. If $u$ is an upper bound of $A$,
then $u$ is an upper bound of $C$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $C\subseteq A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. If $u$ is an upper bound of $A$,
   > then $u$ is an upper bound of $C$.

items.title: Union Is Bounded Above Exactly When Both Pieces Are
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty. Then $A\cup B$ is bounded above
if and only if $A$ is bounded above and $B$ is bounded above.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty. Then $A\cup B$ is bounded above
   > if and only if $A$ is bounded above and $B$ is bounded above.

items.title: Subsets Preserve Lower Bounds
items.statement:
Let $C\subseteq A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. If $\ell$ is a lower bound of $A$,
then $\ell$ is a lower bound of $C$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $C\subseteq A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. If $\ell$ is a lower bound of $A$,
   > then $\ell$ is a lower bound of $C$.

items.title: Union Is Bounded Below Exactly When Both Pieces Are
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty. Then $A\cup B$ is bounded below
if and only if $A$ is bounded below and $B$ is bounded below.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty. Then $A\cup B$ is bounded below
   > if and only if $A$ is bounded below and $B$ is bounded below.

items.title: Union Is Bounded Exactly When Both Pieces Are
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty. Then $A\cup B$ is bounded if and
only if $A$ is bounded and $B$ is bounded.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty. Then $A\cup B$ is bounded if and
   > only if $A$ is bounded and $B$ is bounded.

items.title: Intersections Inherit Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. Every upper bound of $A$ is an upper bound
of $A\cap B$, and every lower bound of $A$ is a lower bound of $A\cap B$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. Every upper bound of $A$ is an upper bound
   > of $A\cap B$, and every lower bound of $A$ is a lower bound of $A\cap B$.

items.title: Differences Inherit Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. Every upper bound of $A$ is an upper bound
of $A\setminus B$, and every lower bound of $A$ is a lower bound of
$A\setminus B$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$. Every upper bound of $A$ is an upper bound
   > of $A\setminus B$, and every lower bound of $A$ is a lower bound of
   > $A\setminus B$.

items.title: Complements Inherit Ambient Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, and take complements relative to
$E$. Every upper bound of $E$ is an upper bound of $E\setminus A$, and
every lower bound of $E$ is a lower bound of $E\setminus A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq E\subseteq\mathbb{R}$, and take complements relative to
   > $E$. Every upper bound of $E$ is an upper bound of $E\setminus A$, and
   > every lower bound of $E$ is a lower bound of $E\setminus A$.

items.title: Supremum Strict Upper Approximation
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above, and let
$s=\sup A$. If $u<s$, then there exists $a\in A$ such that
\[
u<a\le s.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above, and let
   > $s=\sup A$. If $u<s$, then there exists $a\in A$ such that
   > \[
   > u<a\le s.
   > \]

items.title: Infimum Strict Lower Approximation
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below, and let
$t=\inf A$. If $t<v$, then there exists $a\in A$ such that
\[
t\le a<v.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below, and let
   > $t=\inf A$. If $t<v$, then there exists $a\in A$ such that
   > \[
   > t\le a<v.
   > \]

items.title: Uniqueness of the Maximum
items.statement:
Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
$m,n\in S$ are both maxima of $A$, then $m=n$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
   > $m,n\in S$ are both maxima of $A$, then $m=n$.

items.title: Uniqueness of the Minimum
items.statement:
Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
$m,n\in S$ are both minima of $A$, then $m=n$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
   > $m,n\in S$ are both minima of $A$, then $m=n$.

items.title: Minimum Implies Infimum
items.statement:
Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
$m=\min A$, then $m=\inf A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
   > $m=\min A$, then $m=\inf A$.

items.title: Supremum in the Set is the Maximum
items.statement:
Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
$s=\sup A$ and $s\in A$, then $s=\max A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
   > $s=\sup A$ and $s\in A$, then $s=\max A$.

items.title: Infimum in the Set is the Minimum
items.statement:
Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
$i=\inf A$ and $i\in A$, then $i=\min A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
   > $i=\inf A$ and $i\in A$, then $i=\min A$.

items.title: Uniqueness of the Supremum
items.statement:
Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
$s,t\in S$ are both suprema of $A$, then $s=t$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
   > $s,t\in S$ are both suprema of $A$, then $s=t$.

items.title: Uniqueness of the Infimum
items.statement:
Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
$i,j\in S$ are both infima of $A$, then $i=j$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set and let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty. If
   > $i,j\in S$ are both infima of $A$, then $i=j$.

items.title: Upper Bound Property of the Supremum
items.statement:
Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set, let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty, and
suppose that $s=\sup A$ exists in $S$. Then every element of $A$ lies
below $s$:
\[
 (\forall x\in A)(x\leq s).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set, let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty, and
   > suppose that $s=\sup A$ exists in $S$. Then every element of $A$ lies
   > below $s$:
   > \[
   >  (\forall x\in A)(x\leq s).
   > \]

items.title: Lower Bound Property of the Infimum
items.statement:
Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set, let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty, and
suppose that $i=\inf A$ exists in $S$. Then every element of $A$ lies
above $i$:
\[
 (\forall x\in A)(i\leq x).
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $(S,\leq)$ be an ordered set, let $A\subseteq S$ be nonempty, and
   > suppose that $i=\inf A$ exists in $S$. Then every element of $A$ lies
   > above $i$:
   > \[
   >  (\forall x\in A)(i\leq x).
   > \]

items.title: Subset Inclusion Preserves Upper Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq B\subseteq S$ be nonempty subsets of an ordered set
$(S,\leq)$. If $u$ is an upper bound of $B$, then $u$ is an upper bound
of $A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq B\subseteq S$ be nonempty subsets of an ordered set
   > $(S,\leq)$. If $u$ is an upper bound of $B$, then $u$ is an upper bound
   > of $A$.

items.title: Subset Inclusion Preserves Lower Bounds
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq B\subseteq S$ be nonempty subsets of an ordered set
$(S,\leq)$. If $\ell$ is a lower bound of $B$, then $\ell$ is a lower
bound of $A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq B\subseteq S$ be nonempty subsets of an ordered set
   > $(S,\leq)$. If $\ell$ is a lower bound of $B$, then $\ell$ is a lower
   > bound of $A$.

items.title: Supremum Is Monotone Under Inclusion
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above. If
$A\subseteq B$, then $\sup A\leq\sup B$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above. If
   > $A\subseteq B$, then $\sup A\leq\sup B$.

items.title: Infimum Is Monotone Under Inclusion
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below. If
$A\subseteq B$, then $\inf B\leq\inf A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below. If
   > $A\subseteq B$, then $\inf B\leq\inf A$.

items.title: Upper Bound Comparison with the Supremum
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above, and let
$s=\sup A$. For $u\in\mathbb{R}$, the number $u$ is an upper bound of
$A$ if and only if $s\leq u$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above, and let
   > $s=\sup A$. For $u\in\mathbb{R}$, the number $u$ is an upper bound of
   > $A$ if and only if $s\leq u$.

items.title: Lower Bound Comparison with the Infimum
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below, and let
$i=\inf A$. For $\ell\in\mathbb{R}$, the number $\ell$ is a lower bound
of $A$ if and only if $\ell\leq i$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below, and let
   > $i=\inf A$. For $\ell\in\mathbb{R}$, the number $\ell$ is a lower bound
   > of $A$ if and only if $\ell\leq i$.

items.title: Every Element Lies Above the Infimum
items.statement:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below, and let
$i=\inf A$. Then $i\leq x$ for every $x\in A$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below, and let
   > $i=\inf A$. Then $i\leq x$ for every $x\in A$.

items.title: Least Upper Bound Property Implies Existence of Suprema
items.statement:
Let $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above. By the least
upper bound property of the real numbers, there exists a real number
$s$ such that $s=\sup S$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above. By the least
   > upper bound property of the real numbers, there exists a real number
   > $s$ such that $s=\sup S$.

items.title: Supremum Need Not Belong to the Set
items.statement:
There exists a nonempty bounded above set $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ such that
\[
\sup A\notin A.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > There exists a nonempty bounded above set $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ such that
   > \[
   > \sup A\notin A.
   > \]

items.title: Greatest Lower Bound Property Implies Existence of Infima
items.statement:
Let $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below. Then there
exists a real number $i$ such that $i=\inf S$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded below. Then there
   > exists a real number $i$ such that $i=\inf S$.

items.title: Infimum Need Not Belong to the Set
items.statement:
There exists a nonempty bounded below set $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ such that
\[
\inf A\notin A.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > There exists a nonempty bounded below set $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ such that
   > \[
   > \inf A\notin A.
   > \]

items.title: Order Comparison of Suprema
items.statement:
Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above. If every
$x\in A$ is below some $y\in B$, then $\sup A\leq\sup B$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > Let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be nonempty and bounded above. If every
   > $x\in A$ is below some $y\in B$, then $\sup A\leq\sup B$.

items.title: Archimedean Property
items.statement: For every real number $x$, there exists a natural number $n$ such that $n>x$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every real number $x$, there exists a natural number $n$ such that $n>x$.

items.title: Archimedean Reciprocal Form
items.statement:
For every real number $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a natural number
$n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
\[
0<\frac{1}{n}<\varepsilon.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every real number $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a natural number
   > $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
   > \[
   > 0<\frac{1}{n}<\varepsilon.
   > \]

items.title: Archimedean Scaling Form
items.statement: For every $x>0$ and every $y\in\mathbb{R}$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $nx>y$.
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x>0$ and every $y\in\mathbb{R}$, there exists $n\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $nx>y$.

items.title: Integer Part Lemma
items.statement:
For every real number $x\in\mathbb{R}$, there exists an integer
$m\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
\[
m\le x<m+1.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every real number $x\in\mathbb{R}$, there exists an integer
   > $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
   > \[
   > m\le x<m+1.
   > \]

items.title: Archimedean Integer Part Lemma
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, there exists $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
\[
m-1\le x<m.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, there exists $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
   > \[
   > m-1\le x<m.
   > \]

items.title: Integer Ceiling Lemma
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, there exists $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
\[
x<m\le x+1.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, there exists $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
   > \[
   > x<m\le x+1.
   > \]

items.title: Integer Above Lemma
items.statement:
For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, there exists an integer $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ such
that
\[
x<m.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, there exists an integer $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ such
   > that
   > \[
   > x<m.
   > \]

items.title: Unit-Length Interval Contains an Integer
items.statement:
If $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\beta-\alpha>1$, then there exists
$m\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
\[
\alpha<m<\beta.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\beta-\alpha>1$, then there exists
   > $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ such that
   > \[
   > \alpha<m<\beta.
   > \]

items.title: Rational Translation Preserves Rationality
items.statement:
If $r,q\in\mathbb{Q}$, then
\[
r+q\in\mathbb{Q}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $r,q\in\mathbb{Q}$, then
   > \[
   > r+q\in\mathbb{Q}.
   > \]

items.title: Rational Difference Preserves Rationality
items.statement:
If $r,q\in\mathbb{Q}$, then
\[
r-q\in\mathbb{Q}.
\]
items.markdown:
> **Statement.**
   > If $r,q\in\mathbb{Q}$, then
   > \[
